title: Optimization of isolated hybrid microgrids with renewable energy based on different battery models and technologies
method: iHOGA genetic-algorithm optimization of PV-wind-diesel-battery microgrid comparing lead-acid and lithium battery aging models (equivalent cycles, rainflow, Schiffer, Wang, Groot, Saxena), NPC and LCOE
outcomes: Realistic Schiffer model gives 7.05-year lead-acid life, NPC 119,458 EUR and LCOE 0.49 EUR/kWh for current system; optimal lead-acid system at 27 C: NPC 104,690 EUR, LCOE 0.36 EUR/kWh, 5.52-year life, 96.81% renewable share; lithium options lower NPC/LCOE (e.g. 56,204 EUR, 0.20 EUR/kWh); simplified models overestimate life up to three times.

title: Environmental rebound effect of wind and solar technologies in the Colombian household sector
method: Merit-order energy model of the 2019 SIN (1 GW wind or solar added) plus process-based LCA, price elasticity (direct) and EEIO with marginal budget shares (indirect); combined and single approaches.
outcomes: ERE for climate change 1.9-8.2% depending on wind/solar model and approach; backfire in respiratory effects (119,469-376,605%); service sectors 27% (combined) and 47% (single) of CC ERE; savings 12.93 (wind) and 10.18 (solar) g CO2-Eq/kWh.

title: Evaluation of renewable energy technologies in Colombia: comparative evaluation using TOPSIS and TOPSIS fuzzy metaheuristic models
method: TOPSIS and fuzzy TOPSIS over 10 renewable alternatives in 7 regional scenarios; criteria weighted by AHP (investment cost, environmental impact, infrastructure, conflicts with economic actors); Likert expert survey, 14 valid of 35 experts
outcomes: Solar PV (A6) ranks first or near-top in most scenarios (TOPSIS 30.19% Caribbean 1; fuzzy 29%); Andean: large hydro 29.55% (TOPSIS), 30% (fuzzy); Amazon fuzzy: biomass 31%; Orinoquia fuzzy: biomass and PV 34% each; wave and tidal lowest (0-6.5%). Methods disagree on hydro vs wind rankings.

title: What makes Colombia's indigenous peoples adopt microgrids? Social acceptance and financial constraints in renewable energy diffusion
method: Qualitative comparative case study using Rogers' diffusion theory; 17 semi-structured interviews, 3 focus groups (16 participants), field observation of 5 sites; 33 Wayuu from 5 communities in no-energy, solar and windmill groups
outcomes: Solar water-pumping microgrids gave strong relative advantage (higher water security, time savings), compatibility with Wayuu culture and low complexity, producing high willingness to adopt; financial constraints (all respondents) are the main barrier, systems mostly donated; windmills depend on strong winds.

title: Optimizing the insertion of renewable energy in the off-grid regions of Colombia
method: Implicit stochastic optimization (cost/LCOE minimisation) with 100 ARFIMA/SARIMA synthetic wind and solar scenarios, IPSE load curve, calibration on three literature cases and a worst-case robustness test
outcomes: Optimal system was always solar PV 22-29 kWp plus battery 74-93 kWh; diesel never selected; capex US$141,127-177,400; LCOE 0.35-0.38 US$/kWh vs 0.86-4.51 US$/kWh for diesel; worst-case unmet demand 10% (smallest) to 0.11% (largest).

authors: ['Matheus, T.T.', 'Farrapo, A.C.', 'Lagunes, R.M.', 'Filleti, R.', 'Garcia, D.P.', 'Lopes Silva, D.A.']
title: The effect of transportation choices for mitigating climate-related impacts: The case of solid biofuels exported to Europe produced by Latin American countries
method: Attributional cradle-to-distribution LCA (ISO 14040/14044), FU 1 MJ delivered to Rotterdam, 11 cases (2 primary data, 9 literature), ecoinvent 3.7, openLCA, CML-IA baseline, Monte Carlo uncertainty, 3 transport scenarios
outcomes: GWP ranged from -287.37 g CO2-eq/FU (peanut shell pellets, Brazil) to 10.219 (charcoal briquettes); 8 of 11 cases net negative via land use change; sea freight main hotspot for AP, EP, ODP, POCP, CED; Colombian palm-oil cases had highest ADPe (up to 2.027 mg Sb-eq) and ODP (2.659 mcg CFC-11-eq); biodiesel plus >32 t trucks cut impacts most; all cases non-renewable CED below 1 MJ-eq/MJ.

title: Microgrids through the Energy-Water-Food Security Nexus in La Guajira, Colombia: Increasing water and food security or jeopardizing groundwater levels?
method: Qualitative comparative case study (EWF Nexus lens): 17 semi-structured interviews, 3 focus group discussions (16 people), and observation at five field sites; 33 Wayuu participants from five communities
outcomes: Solar microgrids and windmills powering groundwater pumping raised water and food security versus no-energy group (no-energy households walked for 20 L trips). Trade-off: aquifer depletion after decades of use (3 of 5 wind FGD respondents, 3 solar users). Solar users needed irrigation inputs.

title: Energy demand and greenhouse gas emissions analysis in Colombia: A LEAP model application
method: LEAP accounting-type end-use demand model, base year 2015, positive and negative scenarios to 2030 and 2050 for tertiary, industrial, housing and transport sectors; UPME/DANE data; FECOC emission factors
outcomes: Total demand 2030: 1,597,675 TJ (positive) vs 1,748,469 TJ (negative); 2050: 2,125,453 vs 2,498,765 TJ. CO2 2030: 108.3 vs 118.5 Mton; 2050: 140.1 vs 150.5 Mton. Transport largest consumer (44.6% of base demand), then industry (29.8%).

title: A techno-economic assessment for fuel cells hybrid systems in stationary applications
method: HOMER optimisation of diesel/wind/PEM fuel cell/electrolyzer/H2 tank/battery hybrid for a 765-household NIZ town (4 MWh/day); 96 sensitivity scenarios on diesel price, fuel cell life, inflation, discount rate, wind reserve, wind speed
outcomes: Selected hybrid (DG/FC/WT/Bat/HT/E, 6.2 m/s, 50% reserve) LCOE about 0.112 USD/kWh, initial capital 2.64 M USD, NPC 6.03 M USD versus about 0.365 M USD diesel-only capex; diesel use 87% lower than base case; longer fuel cell life cuts cost up to 9%; batteries needed when FC life near 15,000 h.

title: Active demand-side management strategies focused on the residential sector
method: Stochastic simulation of a household lighting circuit with automatic EMS, two PV+battery designs, 20% habit-change scenario; CO2 and NPV/IRR financial analysis
outcomes: EMS+PV saves 10% (Design 1) and 19.11% (Design 2); adding a 20% lighting habit change gives 18% and 27.44%. CO2 emissions fall about 85-86% vs grid. PV alone not viable (no payback in 25 years, negative NPV); with 100% PV subsidy payback is 8 (D1) and 6 years (D2).

authors: ['López, A.R.', 'Krumm, A.', 'Schattenhofer, L.', 'Burandt, T.', 'Montoya, F.C.', 'Oberländer, N.', 'Oei, P.-Y.']
title: Solar PV generation in Colombia - A qualitative and quantitative approach to analyze the potential of solar energy market
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Online expert elicitation (14 experts, 2018) plus household prosumage techno-economic model computing LCOE and IRR for PV/battery sizes under net-metering
outcomes: Highest IRR without storage: Barranquilla 20.74% at 3.5 kWp; Bogota 16.22%; La Guajira up to 40.75% at 1.5 kWp (retail price about 0.50 EUR/kWh). Storage only profitable with price drops (e.g. 11.26% IRR at 25% lower storage price). 86% of experts call for more political incentives.

title: The rebound effect on Latin American economies: evidence from the Colombian residential sector
departments: Antioquia; Atlántico; Bogotá D.C.; Bolívar; Boyacá; Caldas; Cundinamarca; Córdoba; Huila; Magdalena; Meta; Risaralda; Santander; Tolima; Valle del Cauca
method: Panel-data econometrics (log-log electricity demand on price, gas price, GDP per subscriber; fixed/random effects GLS), 15 states, 2005-2013, SUI and DANE data
outcomes: National long-term direct rebound effect 83.4% (only 16.6% of potential savings achieved); state values 64.7% (Atlantico) to 78.9% (Meta); higher in interior than on the coast; model R2 only about 9%.

title: New Microgrid Architectures for Telecommunication Base Stations in Non-Interconnected Zones: A Colombian Case Study
method: Six-step microgrid design methodology (load profile, sizing, topology, feasibility, adjustment) with HOMER Pro simulation of PV, wind, battery and diesel backup for a base station load of 90-92 kWh/month; payback and cost comparison with diesel
outcomes: 100% renewable share with zero diesel fuel use; CAPEX 104 MCOP, NPC 126 MCOP, O&M 2.15 MCOP/yr over 25 years; payback 2.01 years; total 25-year expenses 88.4% lower than diesel-only operation (179.75 vs 1551.3 MCOP).

title: Techno-economic analysis and uncertainty assessment of green hydrogen production in future exporting countries
method: Monte Carlo LCOH model for PEM electrolysis powered by ground solar PV or onshore wind at 76 sites (20 in Colombia), 2020 and 2030 scenarios, 11-year capacity factors, sensitivity analysis
outcomes: Colombia LCOH, solar PV: $8.3-10.7/kg (2020) and $4.1-4.9/kg (2030); onshore wind: $5.2-41.3/kg (2020) and $3.0-17.7/kg (2030). Chile lowest ($2.8-4.5/kg in 2030). LCOH most sensitive to electrolyzer investment cost and utilization rate.

authors: ['Gómez-Luna, E.', 'Tariacuri, J.A.', 'De La Cruz, J.', 'Vasquez, J.C.']
title: A Novel Technical Framework for Colombia’s Distribution System Operator with Distributed Energy Resources Integration
method: Qualitative review of international smart-grid standards/models and Colombian regulation (UPME analysis of CREG resolutions) to derive DSO technical requirements (hardware, software, protocols) for AMI, ADA and DER-microgrids
outcomes: Defines DSO technical requirements (physical components, logic components, communication protocols) for AMI, ADA and DER-microgrids; SAIDI about 30 h/year in Colombia vs 10.4 (Brazil) and 13.6 (Chile); 29 distribution operators serving about 13 million SIN users.

title: A Multi-Objective Optimization Model for Integrating Renewable Energy in Distribution System Expansion: a Case Study of Pamplona, Colombia
method: MOMILP (NPV and CO2 objectives) in Python/Pyomo, epsilon-constraint, GLPK solver, 16-year horizon (2024-2040), IRENA cost parameters
outcomes: Pareto front of 10 alternatives: A1 (profit -159,470 USD, 245.88 t CO2; biomass 91.16% and diesel 8.84%) to A10 (-121,360 USD, 94.72 t CO2; PV 61.37%, biomass 34.19%, diesel 4.21%, wind 0.24%, i.e. 839.45 kWh). A10 capacities: PV 25 kW, wind 15 kW, biomass 7 kW, diesel 4 kW.

title: Evaluating demand response through the time of use model in off-grid regions
method: Time-of-use (TOU) and TOU+incentives price-elasticity demand-response models, four scenarios, ARIMA demand forecasting (R), CO2 equivalence
outcomes: Peak-hour reduction 52.5 kWh/day; with TOU+INC daily consumption falls from 941.5 to 738.3 kWh/day (203.2 kWh/day saved); billing savings USD 119.5/day; CO2 reduction about 10 TonEq/year; about 8 gallons/day diesel saved in scenario 1.

title: Prioritization of Waste-to-Energy Technologies Associated with the Utilization of Food Waste
method: Systematic literature review, MIC-MAC prospective method with 20 experts, AHP weighting, TOPSIS ranking, scenario sensitivity analysis
outcomes: Six sub-criteria weighted: social acceptability 36%, GHG mitigated 16.17%, MSW reduction 15.83%, energy production 13.80%, technological maturity 12.95%, conversion efficiency 5.25%. TOPSIS ranking: anaerobic digestion 78.2%, gasification 47.5%, incineration 27.4%, landfill biogas 6.6%; ranking robust to sensitivity analysis.

title: How to cool a warming world? – The potential of photovoltaic green cooling with natural refrigerants in sunbelt countries
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Hourly PV/battery performance simulation plus dynamic economic analysis (LCOE, NPV) of hybrid and off-grid PV-powered R290 split AC vs grid-based R410a base case, 156 combinations
outcomes: Hybrid residential PV-AC advantageous in 11 of 13 countries (not Ghana, Vietnam); off-grid residential feasible in 5; hybrid commercial advantageous in 10 of 13 (not Colombia, Ghana, Iran); off-grid commercial in 4. In Colombia, residential hybrid NPV difference negligible.

title: Review of Financing Mechanisms to Promote Decarbonization Alternatives in Rail and Inland Waterway Transport
method: Exploratory literature review of Scopus, MDPI, Google Scholar and government sites (2015-2022, English/Spanish), 38 sources retained; country case summaries and Colombian mechanisms table
outcomes: 38 sources selected (23 rail, 15 inland waterway); green bonds, PPPs and public works predominated; Colombia uses PPPs, public works, debt, land value capture and green bonds but sustainable financing for rail/waterways is only starting; more academic sources for rail than waterways.

title: The role of energy storage and cross-border interconnections for increasing the flexibility of future power systems: The case of Colombia
method: EnergyPLAN hourly simulation of 2030 scenarios (BaU, storage, storage+interconnection) with pumped-hydro storage, parametric analysis, and MOEA Eplan (NSGA-II) optimisation of cost and GHG emissions
outcomes: Scenario 2 (wind, PV, storage) cuts sector GHG about 67% with RES 89.4%; scenario 3 (plus interconnection) RES 91.6%, curtailment -47%, 61.2 gCO2e/kWh vs 195.3 BaU. Optimal configuration: RES 96.8%, emissions -86.4%, 26.5 gCO2e/kWh.

title: Informing sustainable energy policy in developing countries: An assessment of decarbonization pathways in Colombia using open energy system optimization modelling
method: OSeMOSYS-COL bottom-up linear-programming energy system optimisation, 169 technologies, yearly single-node, three scenarios (BAU, decarbonisation with CCS, without CCS) 2021-2050, calibrated to 2021
outcomes: Decarbonised system cuts carbon intensity 93%, energy intensity 44%, fossil imports 90%; 2050 emissions 7 MtCO2e (DPS) vs 177.3 BAU; net benefit US$70 bn (21.2% of 2021 GDP, DPS) and US$38.2 bn (11.6%, no CCS); power capacity 127-170 GW; electricity share 54-69% by 2050.

title: Clean and secure power supply: A system dynamics based appraisal
method: System dynamics model of the Colombian electricity market (supply, price formation, policy modules; monthly steps, 2017-2039) with five policy scenarios; behavioural validation against 2015-2016 prices (r = 0.9).
outcomes: High-renewables scenario: CO2 44 Mtoe vs 145 for BAU, average price USD 55/MWh vs 65, minimum reserve margin 11%, renewables market share 25%; price drops to about 43 USD/MWh; free market scenario gives negative reserve margin (-10%) and blackouts; renewables raise price volatility.

title: Scenarios for wind capacity deployment in Colombia by 2050: A perspective from system dynamics modeling
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: System dynamics model (Vensim, 2020-2050, annual step) with 2x2 scenario matrix (policy favorability vs economic signal), learning curves, logit technology diffusion
outcomes: Green Democracy reaches 28,849 MW wind by 2050 (about 40% of capacity; 19,894 MW onshore, 5705 MW fixed and 3250 MW floating offshore), 151,493 GWh/year; Renewable Extractivism about 14 GW; avoided emissions 1.2 Mt (vs hydro) and 149.7 Mt CO2e (vs coal).

title: The significance of clean energy, education, and environmental management in fostering a sustainable future
venue: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
method: Resource assessment with 2020-2024 IDEAM/NASA POWER data: Bird and Hulstrom atmospheric transmittance model for solar; wind roses, Weibull/Gamma/Logistic distributions and Hellman law for wind
outcomes: Mean daily solar irradiation about 4,290 Wh/m2 (min 3,400 in December, max 5,785.8 in March); 4.6 peak sun hours/day. Wind speed 2.6-4.7 m/s (mean 3.4 m/s at 10 m), Weibull k=2.2, c=3.8 m/s; wind potential low May-November; about 745.4 Wh/m2/day at 25 m.

authors: ['Guignard, N.', 'Cristofari, C.', 'Debusschere, V.', 'Garbuio, L.', 'Le Mao, T.']
title: Micro Pumped Hydro Energy Storage: Sketching a Sustainable Hybrid Solution for Colombian Off-Grid Communities
method: Qualitative sketching/design study: criteria-based comparison of electrical machines (ASM, PMSM, SESM with VFD or squirrel cage) and three PV+PHS+diesel microgrid configurations, using IPSE/CNM community data and literature costs
outcomes: Induction and permanent-magnet synchronous machines with VFD retained; microgrid configurations C2 and C3 selected. NIZ context: 1772 communities, 97% diesel-only, 71 with 0 h coverage, diesel cost 0.4231 USD/kWh; literature PV+PHS cost 0.16-0.373 USD/kWh.

title: Mapping the sustainability of bioenergy to maximise benefits, mitigate risks and drive progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals
method: Bioeconomy Sustainability Indicator Model (BSIM): 126 sustainability issues scored by likelihood and weighted via stakeholder workshops, with SDG links; applied to 3 UK resources and 2 Colombian coffee-stem electricity scenarios (replacing grid or diesel)
outcomes: Colombian coffee-residue bio-electricity shows net sustainability benefits exceeding risks, slightly larger when replacing diesel than grid; benefits in jobs, income, sector stimulation, infrastructure, energy access. Risks: capital costs and energy-intensive pre-treatment emissions; grid replacement less favourable because hydro is 71% of the grid. Positive SDG influence far exceeds negative; negative on SDG 9 and 12.

title: Procedure for the practical and economic integration of solar PV energy in the city of Bogotá
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Residential PV sizing from monthly demand and irradiance, equipment selection, scenario cost comparison with and without Law 1715 incentives (VAT, nationalization), savings and CO2 estimates, plus PVsyst simulation
outcomes: Covering 10-100% of a stratum-2 household gives savings of USD 29.72-293.27/yr (stratum 3: USD 29.62-296.18); 4 panels and 1 inverter cover 100%; avoided CO2 about 20.4 t in 25 years; PVsyst energy cost 0.06 US$/kWh, PR 84.2%.

authors: ['Rivera-Niquepa, J.D.', 'De Oliveira-De Jesus, P.M.', 'Castro-Galeano, J.C.', 'Hernández-Torres, D.']
title: Planning stand-alone electricity generation systems, a multiple objective optimization and fuzzy decision making approach
method: Three-objective optimisation (life cycle cost, life cycle CO2 emissions, local wealth creation) with NSGA-II-type genetic algorithm for PV, wind, diesel/gas engine and batteries; reliability index per Pareto solution; fuzzy satisfaction method for selection
outcomes: Pareto front of 133 solutions; best solution 109 (PV 700 kW, wind 400 kW, battery 1500 Ah, thermal 1500 kW): LCC 32.9 bn COP, LCE 81.9 MtCO2, LWC 26.6 bn COP, reliability 91%; thermal supplies about 40% of load, PV+wind almost 60%; avoids 4248 kt CO2/yr versus grid.

title: Evaluating the effect of technology transformation on the electricity utility industry
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: System dynamics model (Powersim), Bass PV diffusion, logit technology choice, 2015-2035, four scenarios (environmental policy x RES cost), PV panel size sensitivity, representative utility 'Company A'
outcomes: Rooftop PV 4,400-10,600 MW by 2035 across scenarios; RES share 16-35% of consumption by 2035; residential sales of Company A 42% lower than 2015 (high PV); household tariff rises 0.13 to 0.20 USD/kWh, non-adopters' expense 13% of income (376% with 2 kW panels, collapse beyond 2033); wholesale price converges to 60-80 USD/MWh.

title: Techno economic model to analyze the prospects of hydrogen production in Colombia
method: Techno-economic model (self-developed Visual Basic software) for 100 MW offshore wind, onshore wind and solar PV with PEMWE or AWE electrolysis; NASA/IDEAM one-year hourly meteorological data; LCOE, LCOH, NPV, IRR, 25-year horizon, 8.2% financing rate; sensitivity analysis; compared with a Korean case
outcomes: Onshore wind AWE has lowest LCOH (7 USD/kg); offshore wind PEMWE highest (9.69 USD/kg). At 12 USD/kg payback is about 7 years for onshore wind AWE and over 25 years for offshore wind. Capacity factor is the most influential parameter on LCOH, then CAPEX, OPEX, financing rate. Selling price for 10% IRR about 10 (onshore), 12 (PV), 13.5 (offshore) USD/kg.

authors: ['Solarte-Toro, J.C.', 'Laghezza, M.', 'Fiore, S.', 'Berruti, F.', 'Moustakas, K.', 'Cardona Alzate, C.A.']
title: Review of the impact of socio-economic conditions on the development and implementation of biorefineries
method: Literature review (2015-2021) with country-selection criteria and comparison of LPI, CIP, 3I and socio-economic indicators for four countries, plus woody-biomass case study
outcomes: Colombia has theoretical lignocellulosic productivity 15.72 t/yr/ha and bioenergy potential 550,000 TJ vs technical 35,000 TJ (6%); lowest LPI (2.81) and low CIP; sugarcane mills are the main working biorefineries; large-scale biorefineries judged non-feasible, small-scale modular suggested.

title: Assessing the effect of incentive policies on residential PV investments in Colombia
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: System dynamics simulation (Vensim) with Bass diffusion, wholesale market and policy-cost modules, comparing FIT, net metering and 30% capital subsidy on efficiency and effectiveness
outcomes: Net metering most efficient (20,298 USD/MW); FIT most effective (highest avoided CO2, 7522 MW PV); capital subsidy least efficient (509,616 USD/MW); about 7532 MW PV by 2040 under FIT and subsidy, 7029 MW under net metering.

authors: ['Calderón, D.A.C.', 'Romero, B.E.T.', 'Quintero, A.D.R.', 'Rodriguez, C.L.S.', 'Perez, O.L.', 'Silva, G.G.']
title: Technical-economic evaluation of a portable solar machine of potential use in pumping systems and water purification, through the use of photovoltaic solar technology for non-interconnected areas in Colombia
venue: Periodicals of Engineering and Natural Sciences
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Five-stage quantitative design: site and radiation analysis (IDEAM, PVGIS), ampere-hour off-grid PV sizing, pump/filtration/UV sizing, budget, NPV/IRR over 25 years at 10% rate
outcomes: Daily demand 1.51872 kWh/day; 2 x 375 Wp panels (750 Wp), 2 x 12 V 300 Ah gel batteries, 85 A regulator, 13.6 L/min pump, UV lamp. Total cost EUR 3805; production 545.9 kWh/year; NPV EUR 1789.06, IRR 2%, payback 4 years.

authors: ['Florez-Montes, F.', 'Martínez-Lengua, A.', 'Iglesias-Martínez, M.E.', 'Taborda Giraldo, J.A.', 'Balvis, E.', 'Peset, F.', 'Selvas-Aguilar, R.J.', 'Castro-Palacio, J.C.', 'Monsoriu, J.A.', 'Fernández de Córdoba, P.']
title: Assessing the Impact of Thermal Coating Paints on Indoor Temperature and Energy Efficiency in Colombian Caribbean Homes
method: Field monitoring with 120 datalogger/SHT20 sensor systems in low-income houses (painted vs unpainted controls), daytime paired comparison of indoor temperature, thermal reduction metric and ASHRAE 55 comfort analysis.
outcomes: Indoor temperature reduction of 1.5% to 16% house by house, average 7.19% (about 7% thermal load); coated houses peaked at 40-45 C vs 50-55 C for uncoated houses; savings stated as 2.5% to 14% in conclusions.

title: A Framework for Evaluating Renewable Energy for Decision-Making Integrating a Hybrid FAHP-TOPSIS Approach: A Case Study in Valle del Cauca, Colombia
method: Four-stage framework: resource pre-feasibility (NASA POWER irradiance/wind 2011-2021, IDEAM flow, ICA biomass), 23 resource-mix alternatives for 1000 kW, 9 indicators, FAHP expert weights and TOPSIS ranking
outcomes: Best alternative 50% solar + 50% biomass; biomass in 50% share in all top-5; 100% biomass ranks 8th, 100% solar 15th, 100% wind last; environmental and technical criteria hold 85% of expert weight; Jamundi biogas potential 10.8e3 m3/day; wind 42% below recommended minimum.

title: Clean Energy Transition in Insular Communities: Wind Resource Evaluation and VAWT Design Using CFD and Statistics
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Solar and wind resource assessment (IDEAM and NASA POWER data 2019-2024, Weibull), NACA airfoil comparison, 2^(5-1) fractional factorial DOE with transient CFD (k-omega SST, sliding mesh, rigid body)
outcomes: Solar 5.13 PSH/day (4764.5 Wh/m2/day) for 175 kWp PV; wind 2.79-5.36 m/s monthly means (annual 3.75 m/s); NACA S1046 selected; VAWT power 0.46-37.59 W, Cp 0.15-0.35; at 3.37 m/s VAWT-V1 gives 10.59 W (Cp 0.276), about 254.4 Wh/day.

title: A novel hybrid approach based on fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making tools for assessing sustainable alternatives of power generation in San Andrés Island
method: Fuzzy multi-objective MILP (cost and CO2, epsilon-constraint, GAMS/CPLEX) for 2015-2024 plus fuzzy multi-attribute Delphi with 9 experts and Mamdani inference (81 rules); +/-5% sensitivity analysis
outcomes: Selected alternative A10 (sustainability index 0.778): 5,772 kW PV and 12,892 kW wind, with diesel kept; mix 94.2% diesel, 4% wind, 1.8% PV; total present value 292.58 million USD; CO2 1718.98 million kg (5.80% saving); fuel savings between extremes only 7.09%.

title: Hybrid Electric Vehicles as a Strategy for Reducing Fuel Consumption and Emissions in Latin America
method: Fleet projection with Gompertz model and logistic curves using RUNT (2010-2022), UPME and ANLA homologation data; tank-to-wheel energy and emissions to 2040; environmental cost (NPV); three hybrid penetration scenarios
outcomes: Light fleet reaches about 10.9 million vehicles in 2040. Scenario 1 raises energy use 1.72% (2035) and 2.87% (2040) vs base; Scenario 2 (about 50% hybrids) cuts it 24.64% (2035) and 33.81% (2040); Scenario 3 similar to 2. Hybrids are 0.12% (491 TJ/yr) of fleet energy in 2024, 1.4% (8924 TJ/yr) in 2040. MHEVs give no significant gain.

title: Analysis of IoT technologies suitable for remote areas in Colombia: Conceptual design of an IoT system for monitoring and managing distributed energy systems
method: Needs identification, requirements, technical specifications and conceptual design; comparison of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, ZigBee and LoRa plus Python signal-loss simulation
outcomes: LoRa selected (range up to 20 km, 21.9 kbps, 255-byte messages) as best performer in signal-loss simulation; four-stage IoT architecture (physical, connection, storage, implementation) with monitoring centre in Medellin; could connect about 2 million people in NIZs; no prototype results.

authors: ['Noriega de la Cruz, L.A.', 'Serrano-Florez, D.', 'Bastidas-Barranco, M.']
title: Analysis of the Availability Curve of the 15 kW Wind–Solar Hybrid Microplant Associated with the Demand of the Power-to-Gas (PtG) Pilot Plant Located at University of La Guajira
method: Seven months of daily wind (inverter readings) and PV (equation-based) power data; theoretical power from IDEAM/NASA weather data; energy balance of plant loads (123.456 kWh/day); availability curve via descriptive statistics and probability analysis
outcomes: Plant demand 5.155 kW / 123.456 kWh per day; PV was main contributor, wind complementary; hybrid supplied demand with surpluses except a few days in Nov 2022 and Feb-Mar 2023 needing grid backup; higher ambient temperature reduced PV and wind output.

title: Combining an accelerated deployment of bioenergy and land use strategies: Review and insights for a post-conflict scenario in Colombia
method: Review of Colombian context and Brazil lessons; expert-judgment roadmap (30+ experts); four scenarios vs baseline to 2030 using LEAP energy system model (OSeMOSYS dispatch) and an Excel land use and trade model
outcomes: Baseline energy GHG rises 76 to 223 MtCO2-eq (2010-2030); bioenergy scenarios cut 11.4, 20.3, 22.6, 24.4 MtCO2-eq by 2030 (5-11%); fossil savings 2-8%; with land-use measures abatement up to 280%; biofuel imports needed (bioethanol up to 76% of demand in Scenario II).

authors: ['Tavera-Ruiz, C.', 'Martí-Herrero, J.', 'Mendieta, O.', 'Jaimes-Estévez, J.', 'Gauthier-Maradei, P.', 'Azimov, U.', 'Escalante, H.', 'Castro, L.']
title: Current understanding and perspectives on anaerobic digestion in developing countries: Colombia case study
method: Scopus bibliometric search, BMP literature compilation (29 papers), online/phone survey of digesters in 69% of departments, regulatory review, five case studies
outcomes: 573 Colombian AD papers (82 in 2021); survey found 996 digesters, 79% tubular psychrophilic (about 5700 estimated nationally); BMP 0.03-0.78 Nm3 CH4/kg VS; AcoD raised yield 14-22%; low-cost digesters cut impacts up to 80%; only about 30% of large-scale biogas used.

title: Chemical Process for the Production of Methanol with Carbon Capture (CO2) Integrating the Concept of Electrification by Heat Pump and Use of Renewable Energy
method: Aspen HYSYS process simulation of base-case combined-reforming vs proposed SMR-based methanol plant with DEA carbon capture and propane heat pump; small-scale distillation experiment; gate-to-gate LCA (ISO 14040, IMPACT 2002+, SimaPro)
outcomes: Methanol yield +5% (2.42 to 2.54 kg MeOH/kg gas); energy consumption -30 to 53%; heat pump COP 5.1, ~86% savings on column reboiler duty (850 vs 6282 kW); CO2 vent -62%; global warming -50%, respiratory inorganics -37%, carcinogens -32%, non-renewable energy -34%; output could cover 97% of Colombian methanol demand.

authors: ['Arango-Aramburo, S.', 'Turner, S.W.D.', 'Daenzer, K.', 'Ríos-Ocampo, J.P.', 'Hejazi, M.I.', 'Kober, T.', 'Álvarez-Espinosa, A.C.', 'Romero-Otalora, G.D.', 'van der Zwaan, B.']
title: Climate impacts on hydropower in Colombia: A multi-model assessment of power sector adaptation pathways
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Climate-driven hydropower projections (16 CMIP5 GCMs, two selected, RCP8.5 and RCP4.5) fed into four energy/economy models (GCAM, TIAM-ECN, Phoenix, MEG4C); six scenarios, 24 runs to 2050
outcomes: Dry climate cuts hydropower about 10% by 2050 (up to ~15% without policy); CO2 from power up to 3%; GDP growth reduced up to 0.28%. Under RCP4.5 TIAM-ECN gives ~40% solar and wind; GCAM and Phoenix under 10%. GCAM hydro share falls 60% to 26%.

title: Modeling the road to decarbonization: A high-performance computing approach to electric mobility scenarios in Colombian cities
method: Compound-growth EV fleet scenarios (CAGR 10/14/18%) with regional shares, charger-ratio, job, CO2 and e-bus algorithms in Python on the SC3 HPC; Bucaramanga case study
outcomes: Baseline 14% CAGR: ~85,000 EVs by 2028 and ~98,000 by 2040; ~2,140 chargers by 2030 and ~9,850 by 2040; CO2 savings 32,100 t (2030) and 147,750 t (2040); local manufacturing ~1,070 direct jobs by 2030 and 4,925 by 2040; Bucaramanga e-buses avoid ~105,300 t CO2 by 2040.

authors: ['Correa, D.F.', 'Beyer, H.L.', 'Possingham, H.P.', 'García-Ulloa, J.', 'Ghazoul, J.', 'Schenk, P.M.']
title: Freeing land from biofuel production through microalgal cultivation in the Neotropical region
method: Integer linear programming siting model at 5x5 km resolution for microalgae, oil palm and sugarcane to meet 30% of 2050 transport energy demand under RCP 8.5, with overlap analysis and Dunn's tests
outcomes: Meeting 30% of 2050 transport energy demand with microalgae needs at least 52% less land than oil palm and 67% less than sugarcane; <5.3% of microalgal areas (~1267 km2) overlap rainforest vs 30.5-32.4% for oil palm and sugarcane (16 373 and 22 017 km2). Colombia target: 7.4 Mtoe.

authors: ['Shadman, M.', 'Roldan-Carvajal, M.', 'Pierart, F.G.', 'Haim, P.A.', 'Alonso, R.', 'Silva, C.', 'Osorio, A.F.', 'Almonacid, N.', 'Carreras, G.', 'Maali Amiri, M.', 'Arango-Aramburo, S.', 'Rosas, M.A.', 'Pelissero, M.', 'Tula, R.', 'Estefen, S.F.', 'Pastor, M.L.', 'Saavedra, O.R.']
title: A Review of Offshore Renewable Energy in South America: Current Status and Future Perspectives
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Narrative review: bibliometric survey of 240 publications on offshore renewables (1972-2022), country electricity matrices, resource potential, ocean-space conflicts, regulation, projects and R&D infrastructure for five countries.
outcomes: Colombia has 41 technical papers (mainly offshore wind, salinity gradient, wave); north Caribbean wind above 1331 W/m2 (max about 1700); OTEC 10-19 MW at Santa Marta/San Andres; salinity gradient technical potential 780 MW; no commercial offshore projects in SA.

title: Evaluation of energy efficiency strategies in electric power generation in Colombia
method: Historical UPME/DANE indicators, LASSO regression BAU forecast (MAPE 1.2%), four PEN scenarios (Update, Modernization, Inflection, Disruption) with expansion and efficiency-upgrade models, AHP-weighted TOPSIS ranking of strategies by plant type
outcomes: Disruption scenario reaches 95.3% efficiency in hydro and 61.7% in wind plants, 34% less fossil fuel use vs 2021 and carbon intensity 61.8 kgCO2eq/USD in 2030; wind strategies rank first in TOPSIS, then hydro; LASSO forecast MAPE 1.2%, R2 0.989.

title: Methodology for the comparative evaluation of vehicle technologies in intermediate cities considering electric vehicles
method: Three-phase methodology: SUMO-Python traffic co-simulation of taxi routes, six technical/economic/environmental/social metrics (consumption, availability, cost per trip, 20-year accumulated cost, CO2 per km, social cost), weighted score; 50,000 and 100,000 km/yr, price and incentive scenarios
outcomes: EV vs ICEV taxi in Pasto: 16.67 vs 122.38 kWh/100 km; 27.40 vs 217.75 g CO2/km; 0.03 vs 0.07 USD/km; accumulated cost 51,498.69 vs 108,203.09 USD; EV 52.13% cheaper after 20 years, savings from year 3.9; score 272.73; without incentives EV cost +12.94%.

authors: ['Morcillo, J.', 'Castaneda, M.', 'Jímenez, M.', 'Zapata, S.', 'Dyner, I.', 'Aristizabal, A.J.']
title: Assessing the speed, extent, and impact of the diffusion of solar PV
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: System dynamics model (Powersim Studio) with Bass diffusion and logit adoption, LCOE vs tariff, 2016-2040, three application cases validated by structure and behaviour tests.
outcomes: PV adoption converges to 25-30% of households in all three countries; tariffs for non-PV households rise about 20% by 2040; utilities face cost recovery problems, lowest in Colombia. Colombia inputs: capacity factor 19%, 1 kW system, 0.14 USD/kWh.

title: Role of low carbon emission H2 in the energy transition of Colombia: Environmental assessment of H2 production pathways for a certification scheme
method: Cradle-to-gate LCA (ISO 14040/14044) of H2 pathways with literature inventories and Colombian emission factors, threshold definition after CertifHy/China schemes, mixture-design combinations, sensitivity analysis and stakeholder mapping
outcomes: Thresholds: gray-H2 up to 21.8, low-carbon 17.0, blue/green 4.13 kg CO2-eq/kg H2; SMR 10.33, SMR+CCS 1.96, wind electrolysis 0.84, hydro 1.51, PV 3.88, grid electrolysis 11.32; biomass gasification negative; 2030 demand needs about 1.3 GW solar and 2.6 GW wind.

authors: ['Luna-delRisco, M.', 'Arrieta González, C.', 'Mendoza-Hernández, S.', 'Vanegas-Trujillo, E.', 'da Rocha Meneses, L.', 'Rio, J.S.-D.', 'Castillo-Meza, L.E.', 'Santos-Ballardo, D.U.', 'Gómez Montoya, J.P.']
title: Evaluating the socio-economic drivers of household adoption of biodigester systems for domestic energy in rural Colombia
method: Systematic literature review and thematic analysis; Economic Viability Score (9 weighted factors) validated by 10 experts; Biogas adoption Economic Model combining EVS (0.7) and regional GDP (0.3)
outcomes: Average EVS 65.6 (moderate acceptance); BaEM scores Bogota 75.9, Antioquia 63.5, Valle del Cauca 57.6, Amazonas 46.0; 7 m3 biodigester yields about US$400/year fuel savings; about 50% of Colombia has organic-waste energy potential; only 1% of bovine biogas potential technically exploitable.

title: Refining wind and solar potential maps through spatial multicriteria assessment. Case study: Colombia
method: Spatial multicriteria GIS (ArcGIS) of environmental restrictions and criticalities weighted by 8 expert interviews, plus distributed LCOE (25 years, 8.08% discount rate, Law 1715 incentives); sites with LCOE >100 USD/MWh excluded.
outcomes: Solar PV: over 8 TW feasible, >11,000 TWh/year (CAPEX 0.86-1.1 MUSD/MW). Wind: 35 GW and 176 TWh/year (CAPEX 1.57-1.88 MUSD/MW). Best solar on north coast and inter-Andean valleys; wind in La Guajira and Atlantico.

authors: ['Pabon-Pereira, C.', 'Slingerland, M.', 'Hogervorst, S.', 'van Lier, J.', 'Rabbinge, R.']
title: A sustainability assessment of bioethanol (EtOH) production: The case of cassava in Colombia
method: Scenario-based mass, energy, GHG, water and land balances of four cascades (centralized/decentralized, with/without anaerobic digestion) from field visits, expert interviews, lab tests and literature, plus sensitivity analysis
outcomes: Energy balance -1809 (CS), 90 (CS+AD), -82 (DS), 637 TJ/yr (DS+AD); GHG 5.3, 0.4, 1.4, -0.3 kgCO2eq/L EtOH; water demand 21-23 L/L EtOH; land 0.27-0.35 ha/t EtOH; AD systems produce 3-5 times more energy than demanded under solar drying

title: Sustainability Assessment of Rural Biogas Production and Use Through a Multi-Criteria Approach: A Case Study in Colombia
method: Three phases: participatory multi-criteria analysis (12 criteria, 10 participants, pairwise weighting) of three low-cost biodigesters; 90-day pilot monitoring of a tubular digester with BgMod kinetic model; IPCC Method 1 benefit quantification for two firewood-substitution scenarios
outcomes: Tubular digester scored 8.1 points (C8 low-cost access weight 0.44); average biogas 2.6 m3/d, 0.21 m3 biogas/kg biomass; BgMod deviation 10.4% in final phase; biogas replaced 83.1% of firewood for household cooking and 24.1% for essential-oil production, avoiding 0.52 t CO2eq/month; LPG saving USD 30/month.

title: Innovative Technology Strategies for the Sustainable Development of Self-Produced Energy in the Colombian Industry
method: Scopus literature review (2019-2023, English) of waste-heat recovery in engines and hydrogen production, combined with UPME self-generation data and mapping of contributions to SDGs
outcomes: ICEs are 49% of self-generation capacity; natural gas 56% of fuel; 36% of industrial energy lost (USD 6.6 billion); TEGs cut fuel use about 4%; hydrogen addition reduces CO2, CO, HC and PM by about 30%; electrolysis efficiency 60-80% at about 10.30 USD/kg; contributes to six SDGs.

authors: ['Vides-Prado, A.', 'Mora-Flórez, J.', 'Domenech, B.', 'Juanpera, M.', 'Parajeles, M.J.', 'Bastante, E.', 'Ferrer-Martí, L.']
title: A redesign method for rural electrification projects, case study in Yutaho, Colombia
method: Four-stage redesign methodology: household survey (45 homes), three energy demand scenarios with LPG load profiles, MILP cost optimisation (8 runs: SHS, greenfield, fixed infrastructure), pandapower power-flow with LPSP, deficit/excess energy and DSM
outcomes: Average household demand 741 Wh/day (EDS1), 1094 Wh/day (EDS2), 3334 Wh/day (EDS3); LCOE 1.61 $/Wh (SHS 1) down to 0.65 $/Wh (GF/SHS 3), FI 13 0.67 $/Wh; LPSP 3-19%; DSM lowers shortage probability by 2.65% on average; fixed-infrastructure approach recommended.

title: Photovoltaic solar energy in Colombia
venue: International Journal of System Assurance Engineering and Management
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Descriptive literature review of about 50 papers from Scielo, Scopus, ScienceDirect and others on PV technology and Colombian PV studies
outcomes: Colombian mean irradiation 4.5 kWh/m2/day vs world 3.9; upper La Guajira 3.6-5.9 kWh/m2/day; 32% of territory not in SIN; PV share projected 3.0% by 2050 in some studies vs UPME 13.75% of 3275 MW by 2028; PV mainly suited to rural non-interconnected supply; silicon cell efficiency 4-21%.

title: Industrial decarbonization by a new energy-baseline methodology. Case study
method: ISO 50006 energy baseline via linear regression of energy vs production, with equivalent-production normalisation for multi-product injection moulding machines; GVLMA assumption tests in R
outcomes: Normalisation raised baseline R2 from 0.4788 to 0.9837 (E = 1.4622P + 67.933); machine intensity 0.13-2.3 kWh/kg across 380 references; estimated savings 1106.9 kWh/year, 235,141,920 COP and 213,039 kgCO2/year; potential 1932 kWh/day.

title: A Review of Economic Incentives to Promote Decarbonization Alternatives in Maritime and Inland Waterway Transport Modes
method: Exploratory descriptive review of official portals, 48 port websites and scientific articles in 16 countries; 44 sources and 100 incentives classified into three categories.
outcomes: 100 incentives identified: differentiated port charges 56%, project financing 41%, onshore power fee reduction 3%. Colombian ports (Barranquilla, Cartagena, Santa Marta, Buenaventura) showed no economic incentives or differentiated port fees.

title: Modeling the transition from coal to SMRs in Colombia: emissions avoidance under deterministic and probabilistic frameworks
method: Deterministic emission-difference model (coal vs SMR, 2035-2052, PEN 2022-2052 high scenario 1771 MW) and Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 iterations plus sensitivity analysis.
outcomes: Avoided emissions 82.62 MtCO2eq (deterministic) vs Monte Carlo median 76.04 MtCO2eq (SD 6.58; P5-P95 66.2-86.4). Sensitivity: coal emission factor correlation 0.86, SMR capacity factor 0.51. Assumed coal 935 gCO2eq/kWh vs SMR 6.5.

title: Transition process from fossil energy to photovoltaic energy power of ethnic communities belonging to the natural parks in the Colombian Pacific: A diagnostic study
venue: Journal of Environmental Studies and Sciences
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Community training and questionnaires across housing, microenterprises, schools, health centers and 180 boats; consumption and cost estimation; 2-month outdoor monitoring of thin-film PV technologies; sizing of a portable PV system
outcomes: Diesel generator electricity costs USD 0.26/kWh (86% above interconnected average); household use 109.35 kWh/month for 3 h/day; 100% of homes cook with firewood; no surveyed boat has PV. Proposed 2x70 W CIGS system (135.92 W needed for 560 Wh/day); LED swap saves 29.62%; about 916.2 kg CO2/year avoided per house.

title: Fully integrated CO2 mitigation strategy for an existing refinery: A case study in Colombia
method: Bottom-up marginal abatement cost curve assessment of 40 mitigation options (efficiency, CCS-EOR, bio-oil co-processing, blue/green H2, electrification) with interaction matrix and five deployment pathways, 2025-2050, costs in EUR2018.
outcomes: Theoretical potential 22 Mt CO2/y at 196 EUR/t average cost; pathways give 0.4-11 Mt CO2/y by 2050; DP3 and DP5 reduce 106% and 98% of refinery emissions but only ~13% of life-cycle emissions; bio-oil co-processing ~60%, CCS 23%, green electricity 7%, green H2 6%.

authors: ['Espinosa Valderrama, M.', 'Cadena Monroy, Á.I.', 'Behrentz Valencia, E.']
title: Challenges in greenhouse gas mitigation in developing countries: A case study of the Colombian transport sector
method: Bottom-up carbon accounting model (demand, fleet, fuel, emissions) with BAU vs mitigation scenarios 2010-2050; marginal abatement cost analysis of 20 expert/stakeholder-selected actions (10% discount rate); MEAVE model for electric mobility; MAPS scenario-building team meetings
outcomes: Measures could avoid 8% (58.3 Mt CO2eq) of cumulative BAU emissions to 2030 and 18% to 2050; annual capital costs 0.5-4% of GDP; investments US$6900 M to 2030 and US$26,700 M to 2050; BAU emissions 48.6 Mt in 2030; electric mobility health benefits US$1490 M to 2050; freight reorganisation holds most freight potential.

title: Making use of the complementarity of hydropower and variable renewable energy in Latin America: A probabilistic analysis
method: Reanalysis-driven hydropower dam, wind and solar models for the 20th century, Spearman complementarity screening (<= -0.5), VRE penetration portfolios and probabilistic risk (10th percentile of driest month) by ENSO phase
outcomes: Hydropower in ENSO drought phases up to 50% lower than neutral (Colombia 25-50%); VRE-hydro capacity ratio in Colombia 44%, giving up to 60-70% more driest-month output; 0.098 GWh per MW VRE in Colombia (Argentina 0.218); about 740 MW VRE needed in Colombia for first strategy

title: Financial Evaluation of Alternatives for Industrial Methanol Production Using Renewable Energy with Heat Pump Technology
method: ASPEN HYSYS V12.1 simulation of base case and five alternatives (heat pump, PV supply, electrified reformer, electrolysis) for 70,000 t/y methanol, with CAPEX/OPEX, NPV (8%, 20 years) and LCOM sensitivity to methanol and electricity prices
outcomes: Heat pump plus renewable PV (ALT3) improves energy performance 15%, cuts operating costs up to 25%, LCOM 456-492 USD/ton vs 612-645 base; methanol output +5%, vented CO2 -62%; green methanol (ALT5) LCOM 659-737 USD/ton.

title: Understanding dynamics and policy for renewable energy diffusion in Colombia
method: System dynamics (Bass-type diffusion with learning curves, profitability, LCOE) simulating BAU and five incentive scenarios (tax reduction, FIT, tradable certificates, technical subsidies, combined) for 2014-2030; structure/behaviour validation and sensitivity tests
outcomes: BAU 2030 renewable capacity about 1900 MW (small hydro ~1300 MW, biomass 310, wind ~150, solar 116 MW); tax reduction adds only 2% capacity at 4.75 billion USD cost; TGC +14% capacity but up to 14% higher end-user price; combined scenario +11% at over 10 billion USD; no scenario reaches the 20% RE target.

authors: ['Castaneda, M.', 'Yanguas, P.', 'Corral, F.', 'Ángel-Sanint, E.', 'Palacios, F.', 'Gómez, D.', 'Ávila, R.', 'Cortés, J.D.', 'Oei, P.-Y.', 'Zapata, S.', 'Dyner, I.']
title: Achieving a 100% renewable electricity supply in Colombia by 2030: Dream or feasible possibility?
method: System dynamics model (PowerSim 10) coupled with scenario planning (2x2: policy x society support), expert workshops, 2021-2030 monthly time step, two regions with energy exchange, sensitivity to El Nino and construction delays
outcomes: 100% renewable supply by 2030 is technically feasible under average weather; best scenario (Green democracy) installed capacity 18 to 41 GW (+127%), renewables 84.14% of capacity; 331,808 t CO2 vs 1,094,349 t in worst scenario; 3-year plant delay postpones target one year; needs aligned policy and society.

title: Energy Performance of a University Building for Different Air Conditioning (AC) Technologies: A Case Study
method: Calibrated EnergyPlus/DesignBuilder simulation of a university building with split, VRF, VAV and chiller AC, validated on one month of measured consumption, plus 20-year life cycle cost (NPV) comparison.
outcomes: Split building uses 18,549.6 kWh/month; VRF 9,626.9, VAV 10,173.4, chiller 10,225.4. EnPI 12.67 (split) vs 8.03 kWh/m2-month (VRF, -36.6%); LCC savings 20% (VRF), 16% (VAV), 13% (chiller); about 30% energy reduction.

title: Biofuel production in Latin America: A review for Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Costa Rica and Colombia
method: Bibliographic review of 77 studies (2012-2023) plus Web of Science bibliometric analysis of biofuel publications for six Latin American countries.
outcomes: Brazil leads regional biofuel production and research (228 of 337 WoS publications; Colombia 26). Colombia: 12 biodiesel plants, 7 bioethanol plants, 9 MW biogas capacity (2022), biodiesel B10 blend, 0.4% of world bioethanol; Colombia most efficient biodiesel producer in a 2010 DEA study.

title: Retail pricing in Colombia to support the efficient deployment of distributed generation and electric stoves
venue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
method: Marginal-cost estimation from hourly wholesale data (marginal emissions regression, 2015-2018), welfare-loss calculation, household-level adoption simulation (65,899 survey households), and counterfactual two-part tariffs with fixed charges by willingness to pay
outcomes: Mean marginal cost 9.5 US cents/kWh; marginal prices 6.4-23.4 cents; annual short-run welfare loss US$83.5 million; at US$2500/kW, 12% of households adopt rooftop solar under existing tariff vs 3% under efficient; electric stoves at US$200: under 1% vs 21%; FSSRI deficit US$470 million/yr.

authors: ['Benavides-Castillo, J.M.', 'Carmona-Parra, J.A.', 'Rojas, N.', 'Stansfield, K.E.', 'Colmenares-Quintero, J.C.', 'Colmenares-Quintero, R.F.']
title: Framework to design water-energy solutions based on community perceptions: Case study from a Caribbean coast community in Colombia
method: Action-participation research developing the CARED framework: first and second community visits, community characterisation survey, researcher triangulation
outcomes: Qualitative: severe water access limits (idle desalination plant lacking maintenance funds, diesel purchases), distrust from earlier failed projects, gender-differentiated effects of water/electricity; solar radiation up to 6.5 kWh/m2 in summer; framework first phase only

title: Optimising the insertion of renewables in the Colombian power sector
method: 15-year monthly cost-minimising capacity-expansion model (hydro, gas, coal, solar PV, wind) with learning curves, solved by implicit stochastic and robust optimisation over 200 synthetic hydro-meteorological scenarios, plus sensitivity analysis
outcomes: ISO: demand met ~52% hydro, 34% wind, 14% solar PV, with ~13.2 GW solar and 10.73 GW wind added and no new gas/coal. RO: 37.84 GW solar PV and 2.13 GW wind give 38.28% hydro, 56.31% solar, 5.26% wind and 0% blackouts. Gas and coal should cease.

authors: ['Rocha-Meneses, L.', 'Luna-delRisco, M.', 'González, C.A.', 'Moncada, S.V.', 'Moreno, A.', 'Sierra-Del Rio, J.', 'Castillo-Meza, L.E.']
title: An Overview of the Socio-Economic, Technological, and Environmental Opportunities and Challenges for Renewable Energy Generation from Residual Biomass: A Case Study of Biogas Production in Colombia
method: Narrative literature overview of bioenergy status, Colombian residual biomass feedstocks, digester technologies, and barriers and drivers of biogas production, with secondary-data tables of biogas potential.
outcomes: Theoretical biogas potential in Colombia 149,436 TJ/year and technical potential 53,554 TJ/year, which could equal 25% of 2016 natural gas demand; confined livestock about 50% of that; recommends tax incentives, subsidies, grants and awareness campaigns.

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Off-Grid Photovoltaic Experiences in Non-Interconnected Zones of Colombia: Integrating a Sustainable Perspective
method: Mixed methods: 6 Colombian case studies selected from 78 projects, stakeholder interviews (Mar-Nov 2020), content analysis (Atlas.ti), SWOT, lessons learned, comparison with 6 Latin American experiences, sustainability dimensions
outcomes: Over 44,000 NIZ users have FNCER systems (39,000 in last four years). Isla Fuerte mini-grid fell from 24 h service (2013) to 3-4 h (2020); Múcura 9-16 h with 35 users; El Islote 1-20 h with 80 of 120 households. Eight lessons learned, SWOT and policy guidelines (Energy Access Law, CONPES, ESCO, microfranchise, PAYG, auctions).

authors: ['Balzan-Alzate, D.', 'López-Sánchez, J.', 'Blessent, D.', 'Raymond, J.', 'Dezayes, C.', 'Portela, J.P.', 'Restrepo, E.R.', 'Rendón, D.M.', 'Malo, M.', 'Goderniaux, P.', 'Daniele, L.', 'Le Borgne, T.']
title: An online survey to explore the awareness and acceptance of geothermal energy among an educated segment of the population in five European and American countries
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Online 15-question survey (QuestionPro) of university-educated respondents, end of 2016; 1063 valid responses (Colombia 249); descriptive comparison across countries
outcomes: Awareness of geothermal energy low in Colombia (35% well/very well; 9% never heard). Acceptance of geothermal electricity 84.72% in Colombia, falling to 77.41% with hydraulic stimulation; Colombia acceptance of geothermal production 66%. Key conditions: environmental protection and community safety.

title: An Intraday Market Design for Colombia's Energy Transition
method: Security-constrained unit commitment MILP (GAMS/CPLEX) simulating day-ahead market and intraday sessions with XM real data for two months and 2,267 unavailability requests
outcomes: Four intraday sessions recommended over two (unmanaged unavailability events 36-64% vs 36-90%); co-optimization of energy and reserve cuts production cost by about 1.5% (month 1) and 1.3% (month 2); schedule changes up to ~2500 MW; adjustment mechanism cheaper than tertiary reserve (system cost +7%, +15%, +26% for 500, 1000, 1500 MW).

authors: ['Luna-delRisco, M.', 'Mendoza-Hernández, S.', 'Da Rocha Meneses, L.', 'González-Palacio, M.', 'Arrieta González, C.', 'Sierra-Del Rio, J.']
title: Geospatial analysis of hydrogen production from biogas derived from residual biomass in the dairy cattle and porcine subsectors in Antioquia, Colombia
method: ArcGIS geospatial analysis of manure availability (census data, Atlas of residual biomass), technical-energy potential from BMP and LCV, and theoretical hydrogen yield by biogas steam reforming (stoichiometry and ideal gas law)
outcomes: Technical-energy potential 1,896 TJ/yr (pigs) and 187 TJ/yr (dairy), total 2,084 TJ/yr (91% pigs); 1,223,056 t pig manure/yr; Santa Rosa de Osos highest hydrogen potential at 519.6 million m3

authors: ['Suárez Bermúdez, L.', 'Ramirez Camargo, L.', 'Yáñez, E.', 'Neele, F.', 'Faaij, A.']
title: CO2 transport and storage potential in the Caribbean Sea, Colombia
venue: International Journal of Greenhouse Gas Control
method: Basin screening and ranking (Bachu parametric method, 12 criteria), storage resource estimation for gas fields and saline aquifers with uncertainty ranges, emitter-sink clustering and transport/storage cost modelling (12% discount rate)
outcomes: Guajira Basin most suitable; storage resources 3.2 Gt in best sinks (14% gas fields, 86% aquifers), 177 times annual industry and power emissions; transport and storage costs 3.2-48 EUR/tCO2; shipping dearest except 2.5 Mtpa over 400 km (19.4 EUR/tCO2).

title: A systematic approach for modeling and planning a sustainable electricity system in Colombia
method: Calliope least-cost linear optimisation, hourly resolution, 18 nodes, 11 technologies; validated against XM 2022 data; 2030 scenarios (baseline, fixed expansion, 5 USD/tCO2 tax, full renewable) under El Nino, neutral and La Nina hydrology
outcomes: Validation RMSE 10.3 GWh thermal, 11.8 GWh hydro. Fixed expansion: solar 2%, wind 13%; emission tax cuts thermal by over 50%; full renewable: solar+wind up to 40% of supply, unmet demand up to 467 GWh, LCOE 1.17-1.60 USD/kWh versus 0.018-0.035 in SCN 2-3. Critical-case emissions 28.0 Mt (baseline), 12.8, 10.0 and 2.1 Mt CO2eq.

title: Energy potential of agricultural residual biomass in municipalities of the highlands of the Santurbán Páramo, Colombia
method: Mixed methods: SIPRA data 2009-2023 plus 18-item survey of 28 farmers (Tona, Silos); TEP = area x yield x residue factor x dry matter fraction x LHV with parameters from two literature sources
outcomes: Silos highest TEP (up to 208 TJ/yr), Tona high from scallion residues (discarded bulbs up to 89.02 TJ); potato leaves and stalks >60% of potato residue energy (up to 45.03 TJ in Silos); source choice changed TEP by up to 30%

title: Climate change impacts and adaptation strategies for a hydro-dominated power system via stochastic optimization
method: GCM/RCP climate projections feeding a hydropower capacity-factor regression, Sobol global sensitivity analysis of 7 uncertain parameters, and a two-stage stochastic MILP (27 scenarios) for generation and transmission expansion 2015-2029
outcomes: Climate change cuts hydropower capacity factor 5.5-17.1% (2015-2029); hydro capacity factor, gas price and emission target explain about 96% of cost variance (79%, 10%, 7%); accounting for uncertainty raises expected cost from about 22.4 to 24.6 billion USD (~10%), shifting investment to CCS, wind and gas; EVPI 4.5%, VSS 5.7%.

title: Financial Analysis of Low-Temperature Solar Thermal Energy Storage Systems to Supply Hot Water and Heating for Rural Colombian Households
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Sizing of a PCM (hydrogenated palm stearin) solar thermal storage with evacuated-tube collectors and 30-year NPV cost comparison against electric and propane heaters (7% inflation, 9% discount rate, COP 4,200/USD)
outcomes: STESS capex USD 22,711 (about 30 times the USD 738 of conventional heaters); variable operating cost savings up to 90% vs electric systems; 30-year NPV USD 30,750 vs USD 30,639 for conventional; 700 kg PCM stores 80.5 kWh; 211 collector tubes.

authors: ['Colmenares-Quintero, R.F.', 'Rojas, N.', 'Colmenares-Quintero, J.C.', 'Stansfield, K.E.', 'Villar-Villar, S.S.', 'Albericci-Avendaño, S.E.']
title: Design of an Integral Simulation Model for Solar-Powered Seawater Desalination in Coastal Communities: A Case Study in Manaure, La Guajira, Colombia
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Integrated simulation: IMSdesign for reverse osmosis plant, HOMER Pro for PV-grid techno-economic design, MATLAB algorithm for IRCA water-quality, health and emissions analysis; data from literature, NASA irradiance and Colombian regulations.
outcomes: RO plant sized for 8 m3/day potable water for a school of 500 children; pumping energy 5.91 kWh/m3; PV system load 47.28 kWh/day (peak 55 kWh/day); PV plus grid more profitable than grid-only with very short payback (values in figure); site irradiance 2190 kWh/m2/year.

title: PV energy performance in a sustainable campus
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Monitoring of a 400 kWp grid-connected campus PV system following IEC 61724 (weather station, power analyzer, 15-min data), yield and performance ratio indicators, and PVsyst simulation comparison for Aug-Nov
outcomes: Performance ratio of 0.73-0.78 (monthly PR about 67.7-81% in tables); module efficiency about 19% and overall system efficiency around 16%; inverter efficiency near 90%. North carport subsystem supplied 1.7% of campus demand on average (peak 5.6 MWh/month vs over 200 MWh/month demand) and 100% on Sundays and holidays; simulation calibration error under 2.8%.

title: Effect of climate variability events over the Colombian caribbean offshore wind resource
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Time-series analysis of 39 years (1980-2019) of ERA5 monthly reanalysis wind at 925 hPa (31 km), Pearson correlation with ONI and AMO indices, CDF and Peak Under Threshold analysis
outcomes: 28 lowest wind speed records (<6.81 m/s) found, mostly Sep-Oct; 71% (20) in positive AMO, 29% (8) in negative; half during La Nina; lowest 2.403 m/s (Oct-1990). Wind correlates with ONI (r=0.16) and AMO (r=-0.15); CLLJ core up to 17.5 m/s; median 11.23 m/s.

title: A Methodological Framework for Technology Selection and Regional Implementation of Residual Bioenergy in Colombia
method: Technology review plus national residue inventory by department (2019 Residual Biomass Atlas) and a qualitative departmental compatibility decision matrix; XM May 2025 generation data
outcomes: Residues total 185.66 million t/yr: cattle 52.03%, banana 12.44%, plantain 10.73%. Anaerobic digesters viable in all departments; gasifiers and pyrolysis versatile but need drying. Bagasse gives over 99% of biomass electricity (99.12%), Valle del Cauca 47.56%.

title: Feasibility analysis for the integration of solar photovoltaic technology to the Colombian residential sector through system dynamics modeling
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
departments: Bogotá D.C.; Antioquia; Valle del Cauca; Atlántico
method: System dynamics models with LCOE and grid parity index per socioeconomic stratum, 25-year PV system, NASA POWER solar data, sensitivity to discount rate, exchange rate and subsidies
outcomes: Highest grid parity index in Stratum 1 (Bogota 0.90, Cali 0.86, Medellin 0.96; Barranquilla Stratum 2 0.54); highest savings 71-72% (Strata 5-6, Barranquilla); avoided CO2 by 2050: Bogota 7,106.51 t, Medellin 5,262.14 t, Cali 2,636.11 t, Barranquilla 3,291.52 t.

title: Environmental impacts associated with hydrogen production in la Guajira, Colombia
method: Cradle-to-gate LCA (ecoinvent) of 1 tonne liquid hydrogen via six pathways: wind electrolysis on/off-site, coal electrolysis, coal gasification with/without CCS, grid electrolysis; scaled to 50 kt LH2
outcomes: Wind electrolysis lowest impacts (~6 t CO2/t LH2; ~52 MMC water); coal electrolysis 66 t CO2/t LH2 (~11x wind); CCS cuts gasification CO2 from 31 to 11 t but raises VOC 37%; grid electrolysis most water (~1600 MMC) and methane (71 kg); 50 kt coal-electrolysis adds 3.3 Mt CO2eq/yr vs 0.3 for wind.

title: Selection of environmental criteria for multi-criteria evaluation of energy supply alternatives in Non-Interconnected Zones of Colombia
venue: 2023 Advances in Science and Engineering Technology International Conferences, ASET 2023
method: Literature review of environmental impacts of five technologies, definition of environmental criterion and six sub-criteria, AHP pairwise weighting by subjective consistency matrix, and indicator design
outcomes: Four net environmental sub-criteria retained; AHP weights: intervened area 48.3%, species affectation 27.2%, greenhouse gases and pollutants 15.7%, climate change 8.8%; indicators proposed for each (area ratio, relative abundance, emission factors).

authors: ['Gil, C.', 'Rey-Ladino, A.', 'Wilmsmeier, G.', 'Montes, A.M.', 'Demir, E.', 'Abouarghoub, W.', 'Sanchez-Rodrigues, V.']
title: A simulation-based analysis for the road freight transport decarbonization: A case study of Colombia
method: Macro-level simulation of fleet renewal (diesel, natural gas, electric, hydrogen) to 2050 using RNDC 2019 trip data, operational measures (empty trips, consolidation, eco-driving) and an equivalent annual annuity technology-choice model; moderate policy scenario vs BAU
outcomes: Moderate scenario: CO2e reduction of 13% by 2030 (2.07 Mt) and 47% by 2050 (13.2 Mt) from fleet renewal; operational measures about 19.3%; combined 57.3% by 2050, still short of net zero. Empty trips 59.49% in 2019; hydrogen about 14% of 2050 fleet.

title: Enhancing DC distribution network efficiency through optimal power coordination in lithium-ion batteries: A sparse nonlinear optimization approach
method: Nonlinear programming (SNOPT in GAMS) for day-ahead dispatch of PV and lithium-ion batteries in 33-bus grid-connected and 27-bus standalone DC networks, compared with CGA, parallel PSO and VSA over repeated runs
outcomes: SNOPT reached the global optimum with 0% standard deviation in all scenarios; average reductions of 0.0503% in fixed energy costs, 9.5198% in energy losses and 0.1322% in emissions; 1.4793% cost reduction with variable tariffs in the grid-connected case; 2.46 s average solve time (94.47% faster than metaheuristics).

authors: ['Rueda-Bayona, J.G.', 'Guzmán, A.', 'Eras, J.J.C.', 'Silva-Casarín, R.', 'Bastidas-Arteaga, E.', 'Horrillo-Caraballo, J.']
title: Renewables energies in Colombia and the opportunity for the offshore wind technology
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Narrative literature and regulatory review plus wind speed and wind power density estimation from NARR reanalysis data (1979-2015) at four Caribbean locations and three heights.
outcomes: Wind power density: La Guajira 482 W/m2 (110.8 m), Barranquilla 857 W/m2 (323.2 m), Santa Marta 658 W/m2 (10 m); mean wind speed about 7 m/s; IDEAM estimates (over 1700 W/m2) judged over-calculated; offshore wind complements hydro in dry season; capacity may exceed the 20 GW onshore.

title: Assessing the impacts of low-carbon intensity hydrogen integration in oil refineries
method: Linny-r MILP cost-optimization of two refinery systems 2020-2050 (5-year steps) with BAU, low- and high-ambition decarbonization scenarios, expert survey for technology screening and sensitivity analyses
outcomes: Preferred strategy replaces SMR with PEM electrolyzers on renewable power; biomass+CCS negative emissions for neutrality. Needs 5-6x renewable electricity, 2-2.5x steam, 2.6-4.5 kt/d dry biomass. Viable up to CO2 price 140 EUR/t (medium) and 205 EUR/t (high complexity). Net margin: high complexity -40% short, -5% long term; medium -52% then +27%.

authors: ['Younis, A.', 'Benders, R.', 'Delgado, R.', 'Lap, T.', 'Gonzalez-Salazar, M.', 'Cadena, A.', 'Faaij, A.']
title: System analysis of the bio-based economy in Colombia: A bottom-up energy system model and scenario analysis
method: TIMES-CO-BBE least-cost optimisation 2015-2050 (5-year steps, 40 time slices) with biomass value chains, BECCS and biorefineries; three SSP scenarios x two biomass supply cases (BioLo, BioHi); sensitivity analysis
outcomes: Biomass supplies 315-760 PJ/y of modern bio-based products by 2050; TPES grows from 2 to 2.6-3.1 EJ and fossil share falls from 76% to 35-39%. Mobilising biomass cuts system cost by up to 11 billion USD/y and marginal abatement cost by 62%; BECCS gives 24-29% of cumulative avoided emissions (SSP1). Colombia becomes a net oil importer.

title: Technical and Economic Feasibility Analysis to Implement a Solid-State Transformer in Local Distribution Systems in Colombia
method: Reference framework of SST topologies, comparison with conventional transformers, hourly demand analysis of one circuit with SST model, and financial evaluation (benefit-cost, IRR vs WACC 11.36%) under CREG 015 special construction units
outcomes: SST flattens hourly demand variation from up to 17.3% (avg 8.34%) to about 1.66%. Benefit-cost 0.56 for 15 kVA (IRR -2%) and 1.04 for 75 kVA (IRR 13% vs WACC 11.36%, payback year 6, viable); CAPEX USD 86/kVA (USD 1,750 and 6,480).

title: Identifying barriers to wind energy diffusion in Colombia: A function analysis of the technological innovation system and the wider context
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Extended Technological Innovation System function analysis with six landscape factors: 16 structured and semi-structured expert interviews (May-June 2014) and media-based history event analysis
outcomes: Wind capacity only 19.5 MW (about 0.4% of technical potential). Functions rated low (mean 1.7-2.6 of 5), government resource mobilisation lowest (1.7); landscape factors rated 3.1-3.8, climate change and corruption highest (3.8). Barriers found in every TIS function; policy suggestions per function.

authors: ['Gómez, J.S.', 'Marín, L.G.', 'Morales, H.K.', 'Llor, A.', 'Hincapié, V.', 'Vuelvas, J.', 'Navas, A.', 'Burgos, C.', 'de Lima Tibúrcio, L.S.', 'Silva, P.F.', 'de Oro Arenas, L.A.', 'Rivera, I.', 'Azar, A.', 'Valencia, J.', 'Yasic, N.', 'Flores-Bahamonde, F.', 'Aguila, G.', 'Cebrian Amasifen, J.C.']
title: Fueling the transition: A comprehensive analysis of hydrogen roadmaps in Chile, Brazil and Colombia
method: Narrative review and comparison of national hydrogen roadmaps, regulations, projects and research in Chile, Colombia and Brazil, with a KPI comparison
outcomes: Colombia 2030 targets: 1-3 GW electrolysis, green LCOH USD 1.7/kg, 50 kt blue H2 at USD 2.4/kg; ~10 operating green H2 projects, 0.36 MW electrolysis, 2.08 kt/yr; ~37 H2 projects (13.5% operational); projected H2 cost falls to 1.59 USD/kg in La Guajira by 2050.

title: Myths and facts of the utility death spiral
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: System dynamics model with Bass diffusion of rooftop PV, learning curve and tariff setting under Net Metering; 2016-2035 scenarios of 1-3 kW systems and interventions (back-up fee, net billing, fixed charge)
outcomes: 1, 2 and 3 kW households give 2.5, 11 and 16 GW PV by 2035 (6%, 35%, 62% of generation); at 3 kW utilities recover 0% of costs. Net billing and 70/30 or 80/20 fixed charge cut PV capacity 43%, 32%, 39% and restore 100% cost recovery; a death spiral occurs at about 2 kW or more per household.

title: Power generation mix in Colombia including wind power: Markowitz portfolio efficient frontier analysis with machine learning
venue: Journal of Open Innovation: Technology, Market, and Complexity
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Markowitz mean-variance portfolio with LASSO regression for returns and Monte Carlo simulation on 2010-2022 daily cost series of hydro, coal, gas and wind (El Nino and COVID periods excluded)
outcomes: Minimum-volatility four-resource portfolio: coal 37.4%, gas 31.6%, wind 31.0%, hydro 0.06%, return 0.1016% and volatility 0.804%; without wind: coal 50.1%, gas 49.8%, return 0.04586%, volatility 0.931%. Efficient frontier with wind gives higher return at equal risk.

title: Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats Analysis for the Strengthening of Solar Thermal Energy in Colombia
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: SWOT analysis based on review of scientific articles, laws, decrees, energy balances and institutional reports
outcomes: Solar thermal could give over 1.3 million cold-climate households hot water or less firewood; solar heat in 5% of industry could cut fossil fuel use by 13 PJ; average irradiation 4.5 kWh/m2/day; installed solar water heaters 100,000 m2

title: Renewables for supporting supply adequacy in Colombia
method: System dynamics model (Powersim, monthly step to 2035) of the Colombian electricity market with eight scenarios combining renewable auctions, Hidroituango delay or absence and droughts; structural, behaviour and sensitivity validation
outcomes: A 100% renewable power system is feasible in Colombia by 2035 (or before) with hydro-solar-wind complementarity and reservoir support, without fossil backup; best scenario gives lowest electricity price, highest reservoir levels and low CO2; hydropower supplies on average 40% at renewable peaks and 70% at renewable lows.

title: Energy Management System for the Optimal Operation of PV Generators in Distribution Systems Using the Antlion Optimizer: A Colombian Urban and Rural Case Study
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Master-slave EMS: antlion optimizer (master) with successive-approximations hourly power flow (slave) on 33-node urban and 27-node rural feeders; compared with CBGA, PSO and VSA over 100 runs
outcomes: Urban daily reductions: 2711.57 USD (27.30%), 1047.56 kWh losses (31%), 3472.28 kg CO2 (27.69%); rural: 6521.44 USD (35.16%), 132.95 kWh (19.24%), 6019.45 kg CO2 (35.38%); ALO best repeatability, about 126-142 s run time.

title: A Data-Driven Architecture for Smart Renewable Energy Microgrids in Non-Interconnected Zones: A Colombian Case Study
method: Functional and non-functional requirements, IoT reference model (Arduino sensors, Raspberry Pi, MySQL, web app, Power BI) deployed on a 520 W PV microgrid; sampling-rate and storage sizing; 6 months of data
outcomes: 120 Hz sampling gives 36 B/electrical and 24 B/environmental sample; about 1.368 GB/day (single rate) vs 1.121 GB/day (two rates) for one generator and two loads; processing budget 8.33 ms; uninterrupted 24/7 collection for 6 months; PV generator within limits.

title: Evaluating decarbonization technologies and optimizing pathways in ceramic tile production through life cycle assessment in Latin America
method: Cradle-to-gate attributional LCA (ISO 14040, OpenLCA, Ecoinvent 3.8, ReCiPe 2016) of company-reported energy and emissions 2020-2022 plus BI-tool forecasting to 2030 with 95% confidence intervals
outcomes: Colombia has the lowest emission intensity (3.93-4.13 kg CO2-eq/m2; 4.12 in 2022), about 24 kWh/m2, 85% thermal energy, 68% natural gas, 7% coal; forecast to rise to 4.46 kg CO2-eq/m2 by 2030 without additional measures. Brazil falls 5.07 to 4.07 and Mexico 6 to 5.45 kg CO2-eq/m2.

title: Renewable Energy Use for Buildings Decarbonization Causes Inequity in Consumers? Comparative Analysis of Spain, Mexico, and Colombia
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Comparative case study: same hourly household consumption profile (2873 kWh/yr) with a 2 kW PV kit under each country's tariff (Net Billing, Net Metering, Colombian hybrid by stratum); bills, CO2, affordability (Gini, minimum salary, PV kit price)
outcomes: Bogota 2 kW PV yields 2742 kWh/yr, avoids 346 kg CO2, cuts annual bills 82-86% (EUR 326.7-581.9 to 47.2-104.9 by stratum); payback 10.2 (levels 1-2) to 6.0 years; PV kit costs over 9 minimum salaries. Spain saves 51%, Mexico 93%.

title: Evolution of Real-Time Dynamics Monitoring of Colombian Power Grid Using Wide-Area Monitoring System and High-Speed Big Data Analytics
method: Descriptive account of the XM/NDC WAMS (PMU network, MPLS communications, PI big-data platform) and development of five real-time monitoring applications validated on operating-system data.
outcomes: 150 PMUs across 25 substations; WAMS monitors 5% of NDC substations yet phasor data are 18% of received data; 10 samples/s, ingress latency under 300 ms; five real-time applications (frequency, RoCoF, angle, oscillations, voltage profile).

title: Assessment of Hybrid Renewable Energy System: A Particle Swarm Optimization Approach to Power Demand Profile and Generation Management
method: Single-objective PSO minimising LCOE with LPSP and RF constraints and rule-based EMS for WT/PV/BATT(/DG) microgrids; NASA hourly meteorological data 2023; synthetic household and industrial load profiles; LCA CO2 and job-creation indicators; validated against HOMER Pro
outcomes: Diesel-assisted configurations: LCOE 0.23-0.35 USD/kWh, LPSP under 0.25%; fully renewable: 0.29-0.44 USD/kWh with up to 50% lower annual CO2 and more jobs. La Guajira household best case LCOE 0.2543 USD/kWh, 14.24 t CO2-eq/yr; no-diesel variant about 60% lower emissions at higher cost (USD 190,815 vs 166,855). PSO cost 13.2% below HOMER in Case 1.

title: A Metaheuristic Framework for Cost-Effective Renewable Energy Planning: Integrating Green Bonds and Fiscal Incentives
method: Enhanced LCOE model with ITC, VAT and duty exemptions, accelerated depreciation and green bonds; capital-structure optimization with teaching-learning, harmony search and shuffled frog leaping metaheuristics; +-30% sensitivity on loan and bond rates
outcomes: Fiscal incentives alone cut generation cost 7.74-13.25%; with optimized financing reductions exceed 50% (BESS 16.6 to 7.1, utility solar 16.8 to 10.3, small PV 8.0 to 3.7, wind 12.7 to 6.1 cUSD/kWh); rate swings of +-30% change BESS LCOE by up to 116% spread.

title: Life-cycle Environmental Impacts of Passenger and Freight Transport: a Comparison between the Global North and South
method: Comparative LCA (ISO 14040/14044, Ecoinvent v3.9, ReCiPe 2016 midpoint, 18 impact categories) of seven vehicle types per pkm/tkm, scaled to daily emissions with local travel data for Bogotá and Reykjavík
outcomes: BEV GWP 27.79%, 18.25%, 13.02% lower than petrol, diesel, natural gas cars but 9.01% above diesel bus; BEV highest in HTPc, PMFP, SOP. Diesel lorry GWP 38.35% above FAME lorry. Daily emissions: Bogotá bus 1.11 vs Reykjavík 3.69 kg CO2-eq per person; BEV 4.11 vs 2.19; Bogotá buses lowest.

authors: ['Paniagua-García, E.', 'Perafán-López, J.C.', 'Nieto-Londoño, C.', 'Vásquez, R.E.', 'Sierra-Pérez, J.', 'Taborda, E.']
title: Hydrokinetic resource assessment in Colombia's Non-Interconnected Zones: Case study
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Flow velocity estimated from IDEAM river discharge, level and cross-section data (Q = AV; 327 days) and a Savonius turbine power/AEP calculation matched to local household demand.
outcomes: Mean river velocity 1.14 m/s (SD 0.013 m/s); one 1 m2 Savonius turbine (Cp 0.25) gives ~142 W, 1245 kWh/y (~50% of 2520 kWh household demand); three turbines cover 400 W base load; emissions cut about 94% versus oil generation.

title: Predicting Energy Consumption and Time of Use of Home Appliances in an HEMS Using LSTM Networks and Smart Meters: A Case Study in Sincelejo, Colombia
method: Bifurcated stacked LSTM (4 LSTM layers of 50 units, Keras) trained on 8,784 hourly records of five appliances from one house (70/10/20 split, 50 epochs), compared with a naive persistence model
outcomes: Total test MSE 0.0168 kWh2 (usage-time MSE 4.8922e-7); full-model MSE 0.00461, MAE 0.02384 kWh, R2 0.91282; total-consumption MSE 0.00093, R2 0.6562; naive model MSE 0.00682, R2 0.31174; 1 h window best (72.61 s).

title: Driving the Energy Transition in Colombia for Off-Grid Regions: Microgrids and Non-Conventional Renewable Energy Sources
method: Document and regulatory review of NIZ data (IECP, NEP, UPME atlases), energy-potential mapping, and sizing/cost calculation of three hybrid microgrid proposals (solar-wind, solar-hydro, solar-wind-hydro) for four NIZ typologies
outcomes: NIZ cover about 52% of territory with 193,871 users; 117,317 homes suited to microgrids (116-309 MW). Proposal 1 (solar-wind) cheapest and suited to localities under 150 users; proposal 2 (solar-hydro) benefits most users but costliest; proposal 3 cuts cost for larger groups. Optimal microgrid size 25-50 users.

title: Design of an energy vulnerability index — spatial and temporal analysis: case of study Colombia
method: PCA with k-means and correlation matrix to select variables, weighted vulnerability index from 2000-2019 national and 2011-2018 departmental data, Monte-Carlo uncertainty (10 million samples), GIS mapping
outcomes: National VI 8.64 of max 20, i.e. 43% of maximum vulnerability (uncertainty +/-21% at 68%, +/-43% at 95%); most vulnerable departments are the high-demand Andean centre and north (>50%); regional averages Andina 61.7%, Amazonia 55.5%; hydro reserves fell 4 TWh 2000-2020.

title: The influences of renewable energy, globalization, technological innovations, and forests on emission reduction in Colombia
method: Time-series econometrics (1990-2020, WDI and KOF data): ADF, DF-GLS and P-P unit root tests, DOLS cointegration with FMOLS and CCR robustness checks, CO2 and GHG as dependent variables, patents as innovation proxy
outcomes: Long-run elasticities: GDP +1.60% CO2 and +1.57% GHG per 1%; renewable energy -0.47% CO2 and -0.46% GHG; technological innovation (patents) -0.12% and -0.11%; globalization -0.53% and -0.59%; forest area -7.38% CO2 and -6.81% GHG; R2 0.9882 and 0.9974.

title: Experimental and Numerical Evaluation of an HCCI Engine Fueled with Biogas for Power Generation under Sub-Atmospheric Conditions
method: Modified two-cylinder air-cooled diesel engine run in HCCI mode on simulated biogas (60% CNG/40% CO2) at 1800 rpm, factorial design; single-zone CHEMKIN detailed-kinetics model for boosted intake pressure and ozone addition
outcomes: Stable HCCI needed intake temperature above 320 C; max IMEPn about 1.5 bar; net indicated efficiency about 32%; ultra-low NOx. Model: 500 ppm ozone cuts intake temperature about 50 C (to about 250 C); boost to 2 bar gives about 300 C.
