title: Identifying the determinants of the energy transition in departments in Colombia: an analysis with spatial econometrics
method: Spatial autoregressive fixed-effects panel models (10 specifications, 297 observations, 33 departments) of CO2 emissions on economic, energy, environmental and transport variables, plus Pearson correlations
outcomes: Higher production, mining, homes, energy, gasoline and diesel use, deforestation, flights and cattle raise CO2 emissions; stable forest growth and electric vehicles lower them. GDP-CO2 Pearson correlation: Caribe 0.88, Pacifica 0.82, Andina 0.58, Amazonia 0.04.

title: Multifactorial Analysis to Determine the Applicability of Wind Power Technologies in Favorable Areas of the Colombian Territory
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: IDEAM wind data (59 stations, 10 m) extrapolated to 120 m in Windographer, Wasp energy simulation with Vestas V136, loss scenario, NPV/IRR/payback economics, environmental risk matrix and 14-factor Likert selection matrix
outcomes: Net production 1.82-113.56 GWh/yr across five sites; capacity factors 1.2-34.2% after losses; Viento Libre (Nariño) best matrix score 52, Villa Teresa 50; Toquilla and El Tablazo with no investment recovery; Villa Teresa 34.16% CF but exclusionary environmental limits.

authors: ['Sagastume Gutiérrez, A.', 'Mendoza Fandiño, J.M.', 'Cabello Eras, J.J.', 'Sofan German, S.J.']
title: Potential of livestock manure and agricultural wastes to mitigate the use of firewood for cooking in rural areas. The case of the department of Cordoba (Colombia)
method: Municipal-level biomethane potential estimation (BMP/TMP) from crop wastes and livestock manure using government statistics; firewood demand and GHG emission factors; capital cost of household digesters (polyethylene, geomembrane, fixed dome)
outcomes: 1.2 Mt agricultural waste and 2.2 Mt manure per year (6687 TJ). 26% of potential covers 1334 TJ for cooking plus 390 TJ for electricity. Firewood demand 663,762 t/yr (~6900 ha deforested); biogas cuts firewood GHG to 11%. Polyethylene digesters cheapest: 18.2 M USD for 150,718 households.

title: Thermo-economical performance analysis of a direct-expansion solar heat-pump water heater driven by a photovoltaic array and the electrical grid in Medellín Colombia
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Dynamic simulation in Python (CoolProp) of a PV direct-expansion solar heat-pump water heater with R1234yf, validated against literature data; typical meteorological year, PV 200-1000 W; LCOH compared with electric and gas heaters
outcomes: Validation: max water temperature difference 2.7 C, COP error 3.46%. Annual COP about 3.5; solar fraction above 88%; PV waste about 5% at 200 W and about 50% at 1000 W. LCOH below 0.075 USD/kWh at about 200 W, at least 25% below alternatives (gas heater about 0.125 USD/kWh); PV above 800 W is oversized.

title: The cities and the sun: The grid parity of electricity generation with photovoltaic systems in Colombian households
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Monthly cash-flow financial model of a household PV system (0-12 panels and batteries) vs grid purchase; LCOE, IRR and discounted payback; 20-year horizon; stratum-4 Medellín household; 2018 and 2025 costs; CO2 savings
outcomes: Medellin reaches grid parity: best configuration 0.7 kW without batteries gives 30% bill savings, LCOE 0.11 USD/kWh, IRR 9.1%, payback 8.5 years, 46% of demand. Without sales to grid max savings 10% (regulation adds 20%). In 2025: 0.9 kW, savings 47%, payback 6.7 years, IRR 13.2%. About 193 kgCO2/yr saved per household; 23,500 tCO2/yr city-wide in scenario.

title: Optimal Structuring of Investments in Electricity Generation Projects in Colombia with Non-Conventional Energy Sources
method: LCOE minimisation with GA, PSO and DE over five financial decision variables; DCF with Monte Carlo (1000 runs, 2017-2021 exchange-rate series) and VaR; real options with Black-Scholes
outcomes: Generation cost reductions of 22.6% (FB, 0.072 USD/kWh), 36.7% (USW, 0.088), 49.2% (PV, 0.032) and 49.1% (WP, 0.058) with optimal debt and incentive structure; tax incentives alone cut cost only 3.7-8.7%; USW expected NPV negative (-0.2 MUSD) but NPV with real options 1.1 MUSD.

title: Differences in the perception of drivers and barriers to the adoption of decentralised renewable energy technologies: a comparison between Spain and Colombia
method: Analytic network process with ten Colombian experts (5 industry, 3 government, 2 academia), compared with Spanish model; Spearman rank correlation for expert compatibility
outcomes: Economic factors are the main drivers and barriers in Colombia; main drivers: market participation mechanisms, fiscal incentives, stabilised low energy prices, supply failures; top barrier lack of funding, then techno-economic uncertainty. Colombian government experts' intra-sector driver agreement 0.32 vs Spain 0.85.

title: Photovoltaic energy in Colombia: Current status, inventory, policies and future prospects
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Narrative review and inventory of PV projects in SIN and ZNI by department, plus review of energy policy and Law 1715 of 2014
outcomes: About 5.28 MW PV installed (46% ZNI, 54% SIN); SIN 2.44 MW in 15 departments; ZNI about 2.25 MWp in 23 departments; solar below 3-4% of electricity; radiation 4.5 kWh/m2/day national and up to 6 in La Guajira; PV cost 3.2 US$/W vs 1.9 in Germany; 70% of projects private.

authors: ['Leguizamon-Perilla, A.', 'Rodriguez-Bernal, J.S.', 'Moralez-Cruz, L.', 'Farfán-Martinez, N.I.', 'Nieto-Londoño, C.', 'Vásquez, R.E.', 'Escudero-Atehortua, A.']
title: Digitalisation and Modernisation of Hydropower Operating Facilities to Support the Colombian Energy Mix Flexibility
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Case study of AES Chivor II: IEEE 1043/1553 accelerated-ageing residual life analysis of stator coils, rewinding of Unit 5, new sensors and PLC data acquisition, simple loss-of-profit cost estimate
outcomes: Rewinding raised minimum breakdown voltage from 38.4 to 95.6 kV (~140%); new coils expected to last ~45 years (life 45-50 years); a 3-6 month winding failure would cost 14-28 million USD versus ~1.7 million USD for rewinding; efficiency gains not yet quantified.

title: Techno-economic benefits of grid-scale energy storage in future energy systems
method: EnergyPLAN hourly simulation of the Colombian power sector, validated against 2014 data (<4% difference); three 2030 scenarios (BaU, COL 2030 with 4 GW wind and 7 GW PV, plus 2 GW/10 GWh storage); cost comparison of PHES, CAES and lead-acid batteries
outcomes: Storage (2 GW, 10 GWh) raises feasible wind+solar share from ~19% to 25%, cuts curtailment by 67.3% (to 1.63 TWh), emissions ~67% vs baseline (62.1 vs 195.3 gCO2e/kWh); PHES is the most cost-effective storage, lead-acid the least.

title: Decarbonization of the Colombian Building Sector: Social Network Analysis of Enabling Stakeholders
method: Social network analysis (UCINET 6) of CGBC workshop/questionnaire data: 357 participants, 4 enabler networks (policy, technology, finance, capacity development), 160+ second-level actions, network- and actor-based centrality metrics
outcomes: Four dense networks (density 0.57-0.77; path length 1.23-1.43; 23-35 actors); national government and private sector lead all enablers; centralization highest in finance (0.45) and technology (0.42); five policy leaders joined 47 of 54 actions (87%); actors classed as leading, second-tier, perimeter.

title: Multi-criteria evaluation and multi-method analysis for appropriately selecting renewable energy sources in Colombia
method: Multi-criteria decision analysis (AHP, fuzzy AHP, TOPSIS, fuzzy TOPSIS) with expert questionnaires, solved in Excel, comparing 10 renewable alternatives in 7 regional scenarios; Spearman rank correlation between methods
outcomes: Preferences varied by method and region; Alternative 6 (PV) most often preferred (e.g. SC1: 21.66% AHP, 34% FAHP, 30.19% TOPSIS), Alternative 4 (biomass) and 1 (small hydro) in some; Spearman coefficients from -0.917 to 1.000.

authors: ['Sagastume Gutiérrez, A.', 'Cabello Eras, J.J.', 'Otero Meza, D.D.']
title: The Energy Transition in Colombia: Government Projections and Realistic Scenarios
method: Deterministic Excel techno-economic scenario model for 2035 (biofuels, hydrogen, all-electric) using Renewables Ninja wind/PV simulations for La Guajira, empirical storage correlations and international unit CAPEX
outcomes: Near-total renewable matrix by 2035 needs USD 123-267 billion (36-77% of GDP), 3.6-7.8 times the government's USD 34 billion; scenario 2 about USD 144 billion with palm oil 0.6 to 12.3 Mha; scenario 3 75.6 GW PV/wind and 643 PJ hydrogen; green hydrogen economically prohibitive.

title: Renewables in the optimal expansion of colombian power considering the Hidroituango crisis
method: Robust optimisation of capacity expansion 2019-2032 with 200 synthetic climate series, monthly resolution, four scenarios (Hidroituango completed or not x government open to renewables or not)
outcomes: Solar and wind enter optimal expansion at 2.5:1 (15.5-16.1 GW solar, 6.4 GW wind); investment 0.81-0.93 vs 1.72-1.73 M USD/MW for traditional; 15-40% fewer blackouts; outages 0.8-1.2% vs 1.0-2.1% of demand; current plan insufficient to 2032

title: Alternatives of municipal solid wastes to energy for sustainable development. The case of Barranquilla (Colombia)
method: Ten WtE routes (incineration, gasification, anaerobic digestion, ethanol, biomethane) assessed via MSW composition and LHV, energy efficiencies, NPV/IRR over 20 years, and emission factors versus landfill
outcomes: Energy potential 1,001-3,283 MWh/day; could replace 1-49% of energy carriers (ethanol 20-49% of gasoline, electricity 1.9-12.4%, biomethane 7-26% gas); GHG 46-92% below landfilling; incineration NPV 396-412 million USD; gasification to power/biomethane negative NPV; landfill gate fee 7.8 USD/t.

title: Renewable energy technology diffusion: An analysis of photovoltaic-system support schemes in Medellín, Colombia
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: System dynamics Bass diffusion model with PV learning curve (80% progress ratio), subsidy and feed-in-tariff scenarios 2015-2035, breakeven, cost-benefit and sensitivity analyses
outcomes: Aggressive scheme (50% subsidy, USD 0.80/kWh FiT) yields 1657 adopters and 5.82 MW by 2035 at USD 4.533 M first-year fund; 50% subsidy with USD 0.30/kWh FiT gives highest marginal increase; subsidy alone yields no diffusion; minimum FiT to start diffusion USD 0.30/kWh; breakeven 2034 for aggressive scheme.

title: How capacity mechanisms drive technology choice in power generation: The case of Colombia
method: Qualitative historical analysis of Colombian power market structure and capacity mechanisms (capacity charge 1996-2006, reliability charge after 2006) using capacity addition data and UPME expansion scenarios
outcomes: Regulatory uncertainty and low prices drove a surge of small hydro (95 plants, 643 MW; 387 MW added 2001-2010); post-2006 reliability charge favours coal and large hydro (about 90% of 3420.8 MW auctioned); wind only 20 MW and renewables share 6-15% of 2028 capacity in UPME scenarios.

title: Diffusion of renewable energy technologies: The need for policy in Colombia
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: System dynamics model (Bass diffusion with logit adoption, tariff formation) of residential rooftop PV adoption, with and without batteries, 2014-2028, with structural validation and sensitivity analysis
outcomes: S-shaped diffusion reaching ~6 million adopter households by 2027 in both scenarios; without storage grid tariffs rise to 0.37 USD/kWh (up to 250% higher) and the market collapses around 2024; adoption insensitive to PV cost once grid parity is reached.

authors: ['Tran, T.', 'Da, G.', 'Moreno-Santander, M.A.', 'Vélez-Hernández, G.A.', 'Giraldo-Toro, A.', 'Piyachomkwan, K.', 'Sriroth, K.', 'Dufour, D.']
title: A comparison of energy use, water use and carbon footprint of cassava starch production in Thailand, Vietnam and Colombia
method: Factory measurements and published data for three cassava starch technologies (ST1 Vietnam, ST2 Colombia, VLT Thailand); energy, water and carbon footprint (ISO 14040/44 LCA, SimaPro, IPCC 2006) per tonne starch
outcomes: VLT: 2527 MJ/t starch (77% biogas), 10 m3 water/t; ST1/ST2 electricity 212 MJ/t, solar drying, water 21-62 m3/t. GHG 149 (VLT), 93 (ST1), 105 (ST2) kg CO2 eq/t starch; biogas cut VLT emissions 72% from 540 to 149; Colombian ST2 water 62.1 m3/t.

authors: ['Gonzalez-Salazar, M.A.', 'Venturini, M.', 'Poganietz, W.-R.', 'Finkenrath, M.', 'Kirsten, T.', 'Acevedo, H.', 'Spina, P.R.']
title: A general modeling framework to evaluate energy, economy, land-use and GHG emissions nexus for bioenergy exploitation
method: Technology roadmapping (expert surveys, workshop) plus scenario analysis combined with LEAP energy system model, Excel land use and trade model, economic and external climate model; baseline and three bioenergy scenarios to 2030
outcomes: Bioenergy deployment cuts 2030 GHG emissions by 11.4-22.6 MtCO2-eq (5-10% vs baseline 223 MtCO2-eq); fossil savings 2-7%; Scenario I gives 150 tCO2-eq per added ha; hydro-bioenergy complementarity cuts fossil power demand 5-6% in dry years; biofuel imports up to 76%.

title: Assessing emissions-mitigation energy policy under integrated supply and demand analysis: The Colombian case
method: System dynamics simulation of the Colombian electricity market (2015-2035) with integrated price-elastic demand and supply, comparing BAU, carbon tax (direct/indirect), feed-in tariff and combined scenarios; validated by structure, boundary and extreme-condition tests
outcomes: Versus BAU in 2035, emissions fall 21.2% (direct tax), 13.3% (indirect tax), 37.7% (FIT) and 41.9% (combined); renewables share 6.9%, 7.3%, 21.0%, 21.2%. Ignoring demand elasticity cuts renewable capacity 14.4% and raises emissions 40%. Assumed FIT 60 USD/MWh solar, 25 wind; carbon tax 30 USD/tCO2.

title: Analysis on the economic feasibility of power generation from renewable energy systems in non-interconnected zones of Colombia, study of cases
method: HOMER simulation (NPV, IRR, energy cost, recovery time) of PV, small wind and small hydro for minimum/maximum household demand under subsidized and unsubsidized scenarios, 10-year lifetime
outcomes: Minimum payback 6-7 years in all four scenarios; unsubsidized: small wind and small hydro viable (e.g. hydro IRR 16% at Valle del Guamuez); subsidized: only PV viable (Riosucio NPV US$3,618,837); Valle del Guamuez not viable when subsidized.

title: The political ecology of hydropower: Social justice and conflict in Colombian hydroelectricity development
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Political ecology and socio-energy systems framework; analysis of secondary data on 13 hydropower plants (1980-2010) across three historical periods, identifying actors, rationales and tools in eco-distributive conflicts
outcomes: Three periods of conflict identified (1970-89, 1990-99, 2000-15). Central issue is ownership and control of territory. About 30% of installed capacity has displaced about 23,675 peasant, indigenous and Afro-Colombian people; 92% of the ~1.5 million Colombians without electricity live in rural areas.

authors: ['Diego Adolfo Mejía-Giraldo', 'Gregorio Velásquez-Gomez', 'Nicolás Muñóz-Galeano', 'Juan Bernardo Cano-Quintero', 'Santiago Lemos-Cano']
title: A BESS Sizing Strategy for Primary Frequency Regulation Support of Solar Photovoltaic Plants
method: Optimization model (GAMS/CPLEX) with an SoC penalty function plus a MATLAB performance assessment algorithm, applied to a 10 MW solar PV plant using 10,819,703 XM frequency records (Dec 2014-Apr 2016).
outcomes: The 546-kWh BESS was the most cost-effective option (about four replacements over 25 years); designs of 546 kWh or more incur no penalty cost; a 300-kWh BESS lasts four years (seven replacements); around 110 kWh penalty cost exceeds USD 20,000 over 25 years.

title: Performance evaluation of external fired hybrid solar gas-turbine power plant in Colombia using energy and exergy methods
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Thermodynamic energy and exergy model of hybrid solar closed-Brayton CSP plant in Modelica/Dymola, hourly DNI model, validation with Solugas plant data
outcomes: Overall plant efficiency 35% without solar input falling to 30% at midday; daily fuel saving 9.21% (max radiation) to 6.3% (min); combustion chamber exergy destruction fraction up to 0.58; heat exchanger effectiveness 0.94 vs 0.98 cuts power about 12%.

authors: ['Cristian Hoyos-Velandia', 'Lina Ramirez-Hurtado', 'Jaime Quintero-Restrepo', 'Ricardo Moreno Chuquen', 'Francisco M. Gonzalez-longatt']
title: Cost Functions for Generation Dispatching in Microgrids for Non-Interconnected Zones in Colombia
method: DC-based optimal power flow with detailed cost functions for diesel, biomass, hydro, solar, wind and battery storage; 24 h dispatch on three five-bus topologies solved with Gurobi/JuMP
outcomes: Optimal dispatch cost of 25,240, 24,278 and 26,143 COP (189, 182 and 196 COP/kWh) for topologies 1-3 versus 518 COP/kWh for the traditional grid (69,000 COP); topology 2 had lowest cost; batteries charge on renewable surplus and discharge at evening peak.

authors: ['Juan Felipe Parra', 'Jessica Arias-Gaviria', 'Yris Olaya', 'Erik Larsen', 'Santiago Arango‐Aramburo']
title: Quantifying the 2050 scenarios for Colombia's electricity sector transition
method: System dynamics model with seven technologies and five regions (capacity expansion, merit-order dispatch, reservoir dynamics, logit investment allocation), calibrated 2001-2014 and tested 2014-2021; four 2x2 scenarios (policy support x economic/fuel prices) to 2050
outcomes: Full decarbonization of electricity by 2050 is feasible in three of four scenarios (Chess, Snakes & ladders, Monopoly); fossil share falls below 7% or is phased out; solar and wind 23-26% of generation (33-35 TWh/yr) and 45-55% of capacity; thermal capacity remains 5-17% in 2050; prices up to five times lower.

authors: ['Juan David Molina', 'Luisa F. Buitrago', 'Sandra Téllez', 'Sandra Giraldo', 'Jaime Uribe']
title: Demand Response Program Implementation Methodology: A Colombian Study Case
venue: Transactions on Energy Systems and Engineering Applications
method: Five-stage DR pilot design methodology applied by simulation to three zones with typical consumption profiles, tariff/price signals and delta-DR per time band; benefit-cost valuation (technical, economic, environmental) over a 6-month pilot; sensitivity analysis of tariff ratios, demand response and participants
outcomes: Pilot benefits vs costs (thousand COP): Zone 1 684,358 vs 553,127; Zone 2 559,392 vs 462,766; Zone 3 (ZNI) 306,213 vs 269,023, i.e. benefit/cost above 1 in all. Base case needs off-peak at 70% of base tariff and peak 2.5 times off-peak (Zone 1).

authors: ['José Luis Torres-Madroñero', 'César Nieto‐Londoño', 'Erika Arenas Castiblanco', 'Zulamita Zapata-Benabithe', 'Hussam Jouhara']
title: Multi-objective optimisation of hybrid renewable energy systems for Colombian non-interconnected zones
method: Multi-objective particle swarm optimisation of wind-PV-battery sizing minimising LCOE, LPSP (4% limit) and life-cycle CO2e over 8,760 h, with weight sensitivity analysis (WSA1-3) on four wind-resource cases
outcomes: Environmental priority: LCOE 0.754 USD/kWh, 18.97 tCO2e/yr, 32 turbines, 98 PV panels, 832 batteries, wind share 90.2%; economic priority: 0.514 USD/kWh, 29.94 tCO2e/yr, 19 turbines, 554 panels, 601 batteries, wind 49.1%

authors: ['Yimy Edisson García Vera', 'Rodolfo Dufo‐López', 'José Luis Bernal-Agustín']
title: Techno-Economic Feasibility Analysis through Optimization Strategies and Load Shifting in Isolated Hybrid Microgrids with Renewable Energy for the Non-Interconnected Zone (NIZ) of Colombia
departments: Chocó; Amazonas; Nariño; Guaviare; La Guajira; San Andrés y Providencia
method: iHOGA genetic-algorithm techno-economic optimisation of PV/wind/diesel/hydro microgrids with lead-acid or lithium batteries, current versus demand-side-managed load profiles, 25-year horizon, 7% interest
outcomes: Optimal hybrid systems cut LCOE versus current diesel supply (Providencia up to 83% lower; Guacamayas 0.08 EUR/kWh); load shifting reduced NPC by about 50% in Titumate, Santa Rosa and Puerto Estrella; lithium competitive with lead-acid.

title: A Comprehensive Method for Designing Containerized Microgids in Non-Interconnected Zones
venue: Transactions on Energy Systems and Engineering Applications
method: Five-step design (requirements, preliminary studies, equipment selection, SoC-based state-machine control, LCOE); 20 ft container with 60x490 W PV, 6x6.5 kW inverters, 28 US3000 batteries, 6.6 kW diesel; load of 50 users; 3 irradiance scenarios
outcomes: LCOE 1,087.69 (Chocó), 857.15 (La Guajira) and 867.42 (Guainía) COP/kWh at 11.07% WACC; diesel supplies 318,249, 96,599 and 99,296 kWh versus 550,859-893,159 kWh from PV and batteries; final battery SoC 28% in worst case.

authors: ['Derlyn Franco', 'Juan Carlos Osorio Gómez', 'Diego Fernando Manotas Duque']
title: Dynamic Modelling of the Natural Gas Market in Colombia in the Framework of a Sustainable Energy Transition
method: System Dynamics (causal loop and Forrester diagrams, Vensim) integrating gas demand (six sectors) and supply, validated against 2018+ data, 12 scenarios with hydrogen, wind, solar and Sirius-2 reserves, compared with UPME projections
outcomes: Reserves (R/P 5.9 years) depleted by mid-2030; domestic gas covers 100% of demand only until 2H 2026. Hydrogen, wind and solar can extend full coverage up to 2033 (Scenario 11); scenarios adding Sirius-2 and solar (10, 12) cover demand through 2035.

title: Innovative Microgrid Services and Applications in Electric Grids: Enhancing Energy Management and Grid Integration
method: Scopus bibliometric analysis, characterisation of 12 microgrid services, qualitative grid-indicator assessment, and review of eight international microgrid case studies selected from sixty
outcomes: Twelve microgrid services classified (conventional, pilot, under development); all are applicable to the NIS and 46.66% to non-interconnected zones; over half improve efficiency, reliability and stability, about 30% resilience; case studies show e.g. USD 800,000/month savings (UC San Diego), 47% less diesel energy (El Hierro).

authors: ['Santiago Céspedes', 'Natalia Cano', 'Gordon Foo', 'David Jaramillo', 'Daniel Martinez', 'Manuel Gutiérrez', 'Javier Pataquiba', 'Juan Rojas', 'Farid B. Cortés', 'Camilo A. Franco']
title: Technical and Environmental Feasibility Study of the Co-Production of Crude Oil and Electrical Energy from Geothermal Resources: First Field Trial in Colombia
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Exergy and energy assessment of produced-water heat, ORC field pilot monitoring, and life cycle carbon footprint (IPCC 2013, Umberto/Ecoinvent) with four fuel-substitution scenarios using one month of 2019 fuel data
outcomes: Maximum potential 2260 kWe (OFA) and 657 kWe (OFB); pilot peaked at 77 kWe, real efficiency 3-6%, mean exergy efficiency 23%; carbon footprint cut 19% (OFA) and 11% (OFB); Scenario 1 (diesel replaced by purchased gas) gives up to 54% reduction in OFB.

authors: ['Sebastian Felipe Castellanos Buitrago', 'Pablo Duque', 'Walter M. Villa-Acevedo', 'Nicolás Muñóz-Galeano', 'Jesus Maria Lopez Lezama']
title: Enhancing Energy Microgrid Sizing: A Multiyear Optimization Approach with Uncertainty Considerations for Optimal Design
method: Multi-year deterministic and stochastic microgrid sizing (LCOE objective) solved by iterated local search with MILP optimisation or dispatch simulation; Python/Pyomo; UPME load data
outcomes: ILS-optimisation takes 4 min per iteration vs 0.625 s for ILS-simulation; tax incentives raised wind share from 10% to 19%; stochastic models give lower LCOE than deterministic; multi-year models more conservative, costlier and more sensitive to data changes.

title: Hybrid Energy Systems Sizing for the Colombian Context: A Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization Approach
method: Hybrid wind-PV-battery sizing with genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimization (Python), objectives LPSP, TAC and LCOE, three demand cases (3.6, 4.27 and 156.15 kWh/day), 25 runs per factor combination
outcomes: Case I (3.6 kWh/day): one 1 kW turbine + 1 battery, LPSPmax -0.007%, TAC 803.90 USD, LCOE 0.524 USD/kWh; lowest LCOE 0.161 USD/kWh with PV. Case III (156.15 kWh/day): 13/13/16 turbines + 100 batteries, TAC 75,560 USD, LCOE 0.392; min LCOE 0.236. PSO gives better-adjusted, cheaper configurations.

authors: ['Grace Quiceno', 'Claudia Álvarez', 'Raúl Ávila', 'Oscar A. Ruiz Fernández', 'Carlos Jaime Franco', 'Martin Horacio Kunc', 'Isaac Dyner']
title: Scenario analysis for strategy design: A case study of the Colombian electricity industry
method: Practitioner workshops (about 25 participants from several Colombian utilities) combining scenario planning, PESTEL, cross-impact ranking, SWOT and causal-loop systems thinking to build four 2030 scenarios and a robust strategy
outcomes: Cost of technology and policy/regulation were ranked the major driving forces; four 2030 scenarios built, with high-renewables/favourable-policy scenario most challenging for incumbents. Robust strategy: entrepreneurial and efficiency skills, R&D for existing infrastructure, monitoring of technology and regulation.

authors: ['Sandra Giraldo', 'David la Rotta', 'César Nieto‐Londoño', 'Rafael E. Vásquez', 'Ana Escudero-Atehortúa']
title: Digital Transformation of Energy Companies: A Colombian Case Study
method: Single-company case report of a 14-step digital transformation (diagnosis, maturity assessment, platform with RPA, big data, cloud, AI analytics, change management) with before/after time comparisons
outcomes: Price-projection simulation time fell from 54 h to 9.6 h; monthly report generation from 108 to about 32 h; offer projection requirements from 76 to 30 h/month; automated contract review, scenario simulation and settlement reports.

authors: ['Cristian Antonio Pedraza Yepes', 'Kevin Enrique Berdugo-Rolong', 'Daniel Eduardo Ruiz-Muñoz', 'Óscar Fabián Higuera Cobos', 'José Daniel Hernández-Vásquez']
title: Feasibility Study for the Implementation of Photovoltaic Panels in Public Transportation in Barranquilla
technology_group: Renewable generation (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean)
method: Feasibility study: PV and battery sizing (IDAE, Sandia methods) for a bus air-conditioner with IDEAM irradiation, SolidWorks static stress analysis of chassis and bodywork, and 30-year NPV/IRR cash flow based on fuel savings.
outcomes: Required PV 35.73 kW and storage 481.204 Ah; bus roof fits only 3.38 kW (9.46%), so on-bus design infeasible; yard-based alternative (60 panels of 600 W) viable with NPV 22,817 USD, IRR 11.05%, 13-year payback, annual fuel saving about 4364 USD; chassis and bodywork structurally sound.

title: Electrification of passenger road transport to support renewable energy integration: A case study of Colombia
method: Hourly EnergyPLAN simulation validated on 2018 (3% deviation); BaU, COL, PEN, 50% and 100% EV scenarios for 2030 and 2050 plus El Niño/La Niña sensitivity; 12% discount rate, carbon price 150/180 USD/t
outcomes: Full passenger-transport electrification by 2050 cuts system emissions about 35% and costs 40%; 600,000 EVs in 2030 cut 8.7% and 3.5%. El Niño raises emissions up to 38%, La Niña lowers them 14%. COL2050 shows 690 GWh unmet demand; wind/solar capped near 10,250 and 8,500 MW in 2050.
